wingfoil-chart

v0.1.0

wingfoil.ie as an Admiralty chart crossed with an old broadsheet weather report: one paper and one ink, the chart's magenta for the best of something and the focus, a red pen for the one thing that matters, thin ink rules and double-rule frames, Fraunces, Newsreader, IBM Plex Mono and Kalam, and the puffin. Figures over prose, mobile first. Light is the product; dark is a proposed night chart.

sem.color.ground{ref.color.paper.100}surface

The page: one sheet of paper. --color-ground. The background of every page and section root, with the grain. Do not: As a lighter card on a darker ground: structure is rules, not surfaces.

sem.color.card{ref.color.paper.100}surface

A box's fill: the same paper as the ground. --color-card. A Pane, a Surface, a Dialog, a pill's fill. Set apart by its ink rule, not its fill.

sem.color.solid{ref.color.paper.100}surface

The opaque fallback for glass. --color-solid. What glass goes to for a reader who asks for less transparency.

sem.color.sunken{ref.color.paper.200}surface

The paper's second sheet. --color-sunken. A well, a placeholder, a tinted row, the selected hour, a quiet control under the pointer.

sem.color.glass{ref.color.paper.glass}surface

Paper over a photograph. --color-glass. A badge over a photograph (Chip tone glass), and nothing else. Do not: Over the map: paper over the map is opaque.

sem.color.inverse{ref.color.ink.900}surface

The inverse fill: ink. --color-inverse. A pressed toggle, the on segment, the hour flag, a strong count.

sem.color.scrim{ref.color.paper.a40}surface

Behind a dialog, over the page it blurs. --color-scrim. The modal backdrop only, with --blur-scrim under it.

sem.color.scrim-solid{ref.color.paper.a80}surface

Behind a dialog where the page is not blurred. --color-scrim-solid. The modal backdrop for a reader who asks for less transparency, and in a browser that cannot blur.

Glyphs

Principles

The rules of the chart that tokens cannot carry. Tokens decide what a value is; these decide when you may reach for it. Read before drawing anything this system does not already cover.

wingfoil.ie is drawn as an Admiralty chart crossed with an old broadsheet weather report: paper and ink, the chart's magenta, a red pen used sparingly, four faces, thin ink rules and double-rule frames, and the puffin. The site is a map with tools over it, and pages that are read (the spot page, the marketplace, the community). On the map, the map is the product, and everything else earns the pixels it covers the sea with.

The product's single source of design values is ui/theme.css (Tailwind v4 @theme), and its primitives are ui/*.tsx. This bundle is a faithful restatement of both, held equal by the project's drift check (scripts/lint-design-tokens.mjs). Where this file and the signed-off mockup (design/chart/1-the-chart.html) disagree on a look, the mockup wins; where they disagree on a rule (contrast, tap targets, one filled action), this file wins.

The accent rule

One filled action per view. sem.color.accent.primary is the filled action: the ink pill, magenta under the pointer (sem.color.accent.hover). A view has one, or none. Everything else that can be pressed is quiet, ruled in ink, or a link. A destructive confirmation is a dialog of its own, and its one filled button is the warm danger pill.

The chart's magenta (sem.color.chart-magenta) marks the best of something, once: a five-star light, the spot in view, a quantity's bar (sem.color.wash, drawn faint), .ie in the wordmark, a link under the pointer. And it is the focus ring (sem.color.focus): 2px, 2px clear, the same on every control.

The red pen (sem.color.pen, its words sem.color.pen-ink) marks the one thing that matters in a view: a loop round the best hour, an underline under the word that carries the note, a strike through what is off (offshore, sold), and the note itself in Kalam. One mark on a view, two at most. It is never a fill, never a control, never a status, never emphasis.

Warm is not an accent. sem.color.warn, sem.color.now and sem.color.warn-ground mean *this instant* or *this is degraded*, and nothing else. The warm red is not the pen's red.

Wind colours mean wind speed. The fourteen sem.color.wind.* stops are speed bands and nothing else, the same for every rider, and they do not re-theme: 35 knots is the same colour on any paper, night included.

What structure is made of

Rules, not surfaces. One sheet of paper: sem.color.ground, sem.color.card and sem.color.solid are the same value. A thing is set apart by an ink rule round it or under it, as a chart boxes its title and a broadsheet heads its columns.

  • sem.rule.hairline in sem.color.ink frames a box.
  • sem.rule.hairline in sem.color.line divides rows inside it, and nothing heavier.
  • sem.rule.heavy in ink heads a section (Pane kind="ruled", SectionHeading). Most of a page is this, not boxes.
  • sem.rule.double (a CSS double border) runs along an edge: the masthead's foot, the dock's top, a page's foot. Write the other three sides to zero first.
  • The double rule round a box is a 1px ink border plus sem.shadow.frame (three of paper, then one of ink, inset): the chart's box, for a dialog, anything over the map, a popup.

Four kinds of box, told apart by their rules, not their fill: the pane (one rule), the chart's box (the double rule), the pill (a capsule, for what is pressed) and the dock (a double rule along its top). A new thing that fits none of them should be a section under a rule.

Over the map, paper is opaque. Glass (sem.color.glass) survives only as a badge over a photograph, and goes solid for a reader who asks for less transparency.

Shadows are small and warm: sem.shadow.control, marker, surface, dock. Paper lifts off paper; it does not float. Everything at one layer casts the same shadow. No drop shadow beyond these four.

The paper's grain (sem.texture.grain) is a background image beside the paper fill on a section root, the masthead, a card pane, a Surface and a Dialog. Never over the moving map.

The dark hours are shaded with the hatch (sem.color.hatch, a fine 135° diagonal), never left blank and never rated.

Ceilings

Type. Four faces, each with one job: sem.font.family.display (Fraunces: names, headings, the wordmark), body (Newsreader: the few sentences), mono (IBM Plex Mono: every figure, tabular, and every label in tracked capitals), hand (Kalam: the pen, and nothing else). Eleven steps:

  • eyebrow 10px is the floor, for the mono label in tracked capitals only.
  • caption 11px is the floor for sentence case.
  • Per surface: one title (30). Per page: one headline (44), and only on a page that is read; it steps to title under 720px. Per view: one reading (48), the wind speed.
  • A map panel (the popup, a Surface, the dock's head) tops out at lead (19): the spot's name. Its figures are figure (19) or less.
  • A field on a coarse pointer is input (16), so a phone does not zoom.
  • Five weights; extrabold (800) is the wordmark's alone.

Radius. Square, as print is: sem.radius.surface and sem.radius.dialog are 0. A field keeps sem.radius.control (2px), so it reads as a box to write in. Anything pressed is a capsule (sem.radius.full). A rounded box is a mistake; so is a squared capsule. The one exception is the instrument over the map (Button raised): a square box, on purpose.

Tap targets. Nothing pressed is shorter than sem.size.touch (44px) on a coarse pointer. A control drawn smaller grows its hit area instead.

Contrast. sem.color.ink-muted is the floor for words. line-strong and ink-disabled are a stroke's 3:1, never text. The pen's marks are pen, its words pen-ink.

Little text, figures over prose

A view says what it has to in figures, a few words of mono label, and a line or two of sentences at most. If a sentence can be a figure, make it one: 14 g22 · WSW · 6.5 m, not "fourteen knots gusting twenty-two". A figure leads, its unit small after it, a gust raised over the mean (Figure). Labels name a thing in a word or two and never say a sentence. The Almanac (the house voice) speaks in the pen's notes and the odd line of small print, plainly, in British and Irish spelling; the puffin signs it, one a view at most.

Mobile first

Draw at 390×844 first, then let it open at 720 (sem.breakpoint.wide) and 900 (sem.breakpoint.rail). The dock, the popup and the spot page are phone layouts that widen, not desktop layouts that shrink. Demos and patterns in this bundle are drawn at phone width unless they say otherwise.

Don't

  • Don't write a colour, a px, a radius or a duration that a token holds. A missing value is a missing step: add it to ui/theme.css and to tokens.tokens.json, together.
  • Don't put a second filled action on a view.
  • Don't use the pen for more than the one thing that matters, or as a fill, a control, a status or emphasis.
  • Don't use magenta for "best" twice on one view, or as body text.
  • Don't use warm to make something stand out.
  • Don't use the wind ramp for anything but wind speed.
  • Don't lay a translucent or blurred panel over the map.
  • Don't round a box, or square a capsule.
  • Don't add a drop shadow, a gradient fill or a glow. Structure is rules.
  • Don't set sentences in the mono face, or figures in the body face.
  • Don't restyle the focus ring.
  • Don't let colour alone carry a state: pressed is filled *and* heavier; offshore is struck through *and* red; warn has an icon *and* words.
  • Don't draw a second puffin, or a second headline.

Gaps, recorded rather than invented

  • The faces. The bundle names Fraunces, Newsreader, IBM Plex Mono and Kalam; it does not ship them. The product self-hosts them (ui/fonts.css). The Studio door and the catalog draw them only where they are installed, and fall back to Georgia, the system monospace and a cursive otherwise.
  • The tide curve's line. The mockup strokes it in #3F6E7E, a darker teal than sem.color.depth, which has no token; the bundle draws it in depth over a sea fill until the product rules on it.
  • The wind-range bar of the mockup's spot page (models and ensembles) uses hues that are not in the theme; it is left out of the bundle.
  • Hover on the map's lights (the mockup scales the glyph 1.18×) is not in the product yet; the light component shows it as the mockup draws it.

Rulings

Dated, because an undated rule cannot be told from an opinion. Carried over from docs/DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md, restated in this bundle's names, then this bundle's own.

  • 2026-09-14 — The ramp is derived from the product, not invented. Every colour literal in the map's sources was harvested and clustered.
  • 2026-09-14 — A legend is generated from PALETTE, never restated.
  • 2026-09-14 — Shape carries kind on the map; colour carries the reading. A light says what kind of place by its shape; colour on it means stars or wind, never both.
  • 2026-09-16 — Model identity hues stay out of the theme, inside the forecast chart and the display filter's swatches only.
  • 2026-09-16 — Two type steps for pages that are read: lead and prose.
  • 2026-09-17 — A page that is read stands on ground, its boxes on card. Since 2026-10-05 the two are one paper.
  • 2026-09-20 — Tailwind is the system. ui/theme.css is the only source of design values; arbitrary values and colour literals are refused by npm run ui:lint.
  • 2026-09-21 — The map's filled action stays on the accent (D13).
  • 2026-09-21 — An active filter is a line, not a fill (a border and an inset ring in the accent), so it does not rival the one filled action.
  • 2026-10-05 — The chart. Paper (#f3eee3) and ink (#1a1d21), structure in rules, opaque paper over the map, square boxes, the focus ring in the chart's magenta, four self-hosted faces on eleven steps, and the red pen with its own rule. Measured on paper: ink 14.62:1, ink-2 9.54:1, ink-muted 5.80:1 (5.40:1 on sunken), line-strong 3.66:1, chart-magenta 5.70:1, warn 5.68:1, pen 4.09:1 (a stroke), pen-ink 4.93:1 (words), paper on the hovered accent 5.70:1.
  • 2026-10-05 — No dark mode in the product: the chart is paper. The product ships light only (D9). A night chart (as a chart is read under a red light on a night passage) is a possible later mode. The Studio's Design door requires a bundle to declare both modes, so this bundle carries a restrained night chart as a proposal: warm dark ink paper (#1d1c19, never blue-shifted), paper-coloured ink, magenta lifted to #e6609f (4.9:1+) and the pen to #ef5f4f, the wind ramp, the now-marker, the gust cap and the buoy unchanged. No product surface reads it. It needs its own contrast pass and a dark basemap before it is offered.
  • 2026-10-05 — The bundle's names are the product's. A sem colour is the Tailwind name unchanged (--color-ink-muted is --sem-color-ink-muted), except the accent, which is a group. A handful of interop aliases (sem.color.bg.app, text.primary, font.family.ui, …) exist only so the Studio's catalog and door draw in the brand; components never use them.
  • 2026-10-05 — The map's vocabulary is part of the system. The spot's light, the shore compass, the wind-and-gust figure, the tide label and the dock's hour cell repeat across the map, the dock, the popup and the spot page, and are components here, drawn as the mockup draws them.

Components

Avatar

Avatar

Monogram · sm, md, lg

AN AN AN C SÓ

Photo · sm, md, lg

Beside the name, always

AN Aoife Ní Bhriain Dollymount · 3 listings

Avatar · night chart (proposed)

SÓ SÓ SÓ

A face for a name (ui/Avatar.tsx, avatarStyles): the member's photo, or a monogram in the display face's italic, in an ink ring. Decoration: the name is always written beside it.

Anatomy

  • Ring: .wf-avatar — a circle (sem.radius.full) with a sem.rule.hairline ink border, sem.color.sunken behind, clipping what is inside.
  • Monogram: up to two letters, the first of the first word and of the last ("Aoife Ní Bhriain" is AN), in sem.font.family.display italic, sem.font.weight.semibold, line-height 1, in ink.
  • Photo: .wf-avatar__image — an img with an empty alt, filling the ring and cropped to it (object-fit: cover).

Variants

  • Sm (--sm) — sem.size.control.sm (30px), the monogram at sem.font.size.caption.
  • Md (the default) — sem.size.control.md (40px), at sem.font.size.body.
  • Lg (--lg) — 72px (18 steps), at sem.font.size.title with its tracking; the weight stays semibold. A profile's head.

States

  • No photo, or a photo that fails to load: the monogram stands in.
  • An empty name draws "?".

Usage

  • Always with the name written beside it, in the display face; the avatar never stands in for the name.
  • Monograms over stock pictures: the community draws monograms unless a member has given a photo.
  • Do not colour the ring or the sheet to tell members apart; the ring is ink.

Accessibility

  • aria-hidden="true" on the ring, and alt="" on the photo: the name beside it is what is read, once.
  • Ink on sunken is 13.6:1.
components/avatar/component.css
/* Avatar — ui/Avatar.tsx (avatarStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * A face for a name: the member's photo, or a monogram of up to two letters in
 * the display face's italic, on the paper's second sheet, in an ink ring as
 * everything that stands on the page is. Decoration: the name is always
 * written beside it. */

/* size="md" (the default). */
.wf-avatar {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  display: inline-grid;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  place-items: center;
  overflow: hidden;
  width: var(--sem-size-control-md);
  height: var(--sem-size-control-md);
  border: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
  background: var(--sem-color-sunken);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-display);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  line-height: 1;
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
  font-style: italic;
}

/* size="sm": a row in a list, a notification. */
.wf-avatar--sm {
  width: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
  height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-caption);
}

/* size="lg": a profile's head (72px). The title step brings its tracking; the
 * weight stays semibold. */
.wf-avatar--lg {
  width: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 18);
  height: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 18);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-title);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-title);
}

/* The photo fills the ring, cropped to it. */
.wf-avatar__image {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  object-fit: cover;
}

Button

Button

Variants · md

Hover (held)

Focus-visible (held): one ring, 2px of magenta, 2px clear

Disabled

Sizes · sm, md, lg

Pressed · a toggle that is on, and one that says so in words

Icon · needs an aria-label · the instrument over the map stays square

Button · night chart (proposed)

The kit's one pressable control (ui/Button.tsx, buttonStyles). Mono capitals in every variant; the shape says what it is.

Anatomy

  • Container: .wf-button — sem.size.control.md tall, sem.space.x4 across, a hairline border (transparent unless the variant rules it), a capsule.
  • Label: IBM Plex Mono at sem.font.size.label, sem.font.weight.label, tracked sem.font.tracking.label, uppercase.
  • Optional icon: .wf-button__icon, 16px, currentColor, stroke 1.5 beside the mono label (lucide's default 2 reads heavy against the thin rules).

Variants

  • Quiet (.wf-button, the default) — no fill; sem.color.sunken under the pointer. Everything that is not the one action.
  • Primary (--primary) — the ink pill: sem.color.accent.primary fill, sem.color.accent.ink label, sem.color.accent.hover (magenta) under the pointer. One per view, or none.
  • Pill (--pill) — a capsule ruled in ink on paper; inverse under the pointer. Sign in, Previous / Next, Cancel.
  • Raised (--raised) — the chart's instrument over the map: a square box ruled in ink (the site menu, zoom, IRL, layers). Casts no shadow; its frame does.
  • Link (--link) — the label face underlined in ink, "← Chart"; magenta under the pointer. No box.
  • Danger (--danger) — the warm pill, for the destructive answer in a confirm dialog and nowhere else. Lifts (sem.shadow.marker) under the pointer.
  • Sizes --sm (30), md (40), --lg (46, semibold).
  • Icon (--icon) — width equals height; raised stays square.
  • Pressed (aria-pressed="true") — filled in inverse, semibold and with sem.shadow.control: never colour alone. --worded keeps its quiet box for a toggle whose words say it is on (Save → Saved).

States

  • Hover: per variant above (.is-hover holds it in the demo).
  • Focus: :focus-visible draws the one ring — sem.ring.width of sem.color.focus, sem.ring.offset clear (.is-focus in the demo).
  • Disabled: sem.color.ink-disabled words, default cursor, no fade; filled variants go to sem.color.sunken on a sem.color.line ring.
  • Coarse pointer: never shorter than sem.size.touch; a link grows an invisible touch-tall band instead.

Usage

  • One --primary per view. If a view seems to need two, the hierarchy is wrong.
  • Name the action in a word or two: "Spot page →", "Sell", "Sign in".
  • --danger only inside a confirm dialog, after Cancel in the document.
  • With an href the product renders an <a> with the same classes, announced as a link; a link cannot be pressed, the current one carries aria-current="true" and draws as pressed.

Accessibility

  • A real <button type="button">, or <a href> for navigation.
  • An icon-only button must carry aria-label; the product's types refuse one without it.
  • Toggles expose aria-pressed; the pressed look adds weight and fill, so it survives greyscale.
  • Label contrast: paper on ink 14.6:1, paper on the magenta hover 5.7:1, paper on warn 5.7:1.
components/button/component.css
/* Button — ui/Button.tsx (buttonStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * Every button speaks in the mono label: tracked capitals in IBM Plex Mono.
 * The shapes are the chart's: a capsule ruled in ink, filled in ink when it is
 * the one action, and a square box for an instrument laid over the map.
 *
 * `.is-hover` and `.is-focus` hold a state still for the catalog; the product
 * reaches the same rules through :hover and :focus-visible. */

.wf-button {
  position: relative;
  display: inline-flex;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x1-5);
  box-sizing: border-box;
  height: var(--sem-size-control-md);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-x4);
  border: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid transparent;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-pill);
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-quiet);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-label);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-label);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-label);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-label);
  text-transform: uppercase;
  text-decoration: none;
  white-space: nowrap;
  cursor: pointer;
  touch-action: manipulation;
  transition-property: color, background-color, border-color, text-decoration-color;
  transition-duration: var(--sem-duration-fast);
}

/* A tap target is never shorter than touch, whatever size was asked for. */
@media (pointer: coarse) {
  .wf-button {
    min-height: var(--sem-size-touch);
  }
}

.wf-button:not(:disabled):focus-visible,
.wf-button.is-focus {
  outline: var(--sem-ring-width) solid var(--sem-color-focus);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-ring-offset);
}

/* Disabled is said in ink and cursor, not a fade. */
.wf-button:disabled {
  cursor: default;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-disabled);
  opacity: 1;
}

/* ---- sizes ---- */
.wf-button--sm {
  height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-x3);
}
.wf-button--lg {
  height: var(--sem-size-control-lg);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-x5);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
}

/* ---- quiet (the default): no fill until the pointer is over it ---- */
.wf-button:not(:disabled):hover,
.wf-button.is-hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-sunken);
}

/* ---- primary: the one filled control, an ink pill, magenta under the pointer ---- */
.wf-button--primary {
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
  border-color: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  background: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  color: var(--sem-color-accent-ink);
}
.wf-button--primary:not(:disabled):hover,
.wf-button--primary.is-hover {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-accent-hover);
  background: var(--sem-color-accent-hover);
}
.wf-button--primary:disabled {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-line);
  background: var(--sem-color-sunken);
}

/* ---- pill: a capsule ruled in ink, which turns to ink under the pointer ---- */
.wf-button--pill {
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
  border-color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  background: var(--sem-color-card);
}
.wf-button--pill:not(:disabled):hover,
.wf-button--pill.is-hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-inverse);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-inverse);
}
.wf-button--pill:disabled {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-line);
  background: transparent;
}

/* ---- raised: the chart's instrument over the map, a square box ruled in ink ---- */
.wf-button--raised {
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-surface);
  border-color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  background: var(--sem-color-card);
}
.wf-button--raised:not(:disabled):hover,
.wf-button--raised.is-hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-inverse);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-inverse);
}
.wf-button--raised:disabled {
  background: transparent;
}

/* ---- link: a way back or on, underlined in ink ("← Chart") ---- */
.wf-button--link {
  height: auto;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  text-decoration: underline;
  text-decoration-thickness: var(--sem-rule-hairline);
  text-underline-offset: var(--sem-space-x1);
  text-decoration-color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}
.wf-button--link:not(:disabled):hover,
.wf-button--link.is-hover {
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-chart-magenta);
  text-decoration-color: currentColor;
}
@media (pointer: coarse) {
  .wf-button--link {
    min-height: 0;
  }
  /* A touch-tall band across the words: the target grows, nothing moves. */
  .wf-button--link::before {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    inset-inline: 0;
    top: 50%;
    height: var(--sem-size-touch);
    transform: translateY(-50%);
  }
}

/* ---- danger: the destructive answer in a confirm dialog, and nowhere else ---- */
.wf-button--danger {
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
  border-color: var(--sem-color-warn);
  background: var(--sem-color-warn);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-inverse);
}
.wf-button--danger:not(:disabled):hover,
.wf-button--danger.is-hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-warn);
  box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-marker);
}
.wf-button--danger:disabled {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-line);
  background: var(--sem-color-sunken);
}

/* ---- pressed: a toggle that is on — filled in ink and heavier, never colour alone ---- */
.wf-button[aria-pressed="true"],
.wf-button[aria-current="true"] {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  background: var(--sem-color-inverse);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-inverse);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
  box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-control);
}
.wf-button[aria-pressed="true"]:not(:disabled):hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-inverse);
}
.wf-button[aria-pressed="true"]:disabled {
  background: var(--sem-color-sunken);
}
/* A toggle whose own words say it is on (Save -> Saved) keeps its quiet box. */
.wf-button--worded[aria-pressed="true"] {
  border-color: transparent;
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-quiet);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-label);
  box-shadow: none;
}

/* ---- icon: a square-sized capsule, which needs an aria-label ---- */
.wf-button--icon {
  width: var(--sem-size-control-md);
  padding: 0;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
}
.wf-button--icon.wf-button--sm {
  width: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
}
.wf-button--icon.wf-button--lg {
  width: var(--sem-size-control-lg);
}
/* The instrument stays square with an icon in it. */
.wf-button--icon.wf-button--raised {
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-surface);
}
@media (pointer: coarse) {
  .wf-button--icon {
    min-width: var(--sem-size-touch);
  }
}

.wf-button__icon {
  width: var(--sem-space-x4);
  height: var(--sem-space-x4);
  flex-shrink: 0;
}

Checkbox

Checkbox

Checked, unchecked · the chart's layers

Focus-visible (held)

Disabled

Checkbox · night chart (proposed)

One thing that is either so or not, with the words that say which (ui/Checkbox.tsx, checkboxStyles). The platform's own box and tick, the words part of the target.

Anatomy

  • Row: .wf-checkbox on a <label> — an inline row at least sem.size.touch tall, sem.space.x2 between box and words, Newsreader at sem.font.size.prose in sem.color.ink. The whole row turns the box on.
  • Box: .wf-checkbox__input on an <input type="checkbox"> — the platform's box, sem.space.step × 4.5 (18) square, no margin, its fill and tick in accent-color: sem.color.inverse.
  • Words: .wf-checkbox__label on a <span> — may wrap, never pushes the box out (min-width: 0).

Variants

  • One. A row of them is a ruled list or a plain column, as the chart's layers panel draws them.

States

  • Checked: the platform's tick on an ink fill; unchecked, the platform's empty box. The tick is what says checked, a mark that is there or not.
  • Focus: :focus-visible draws the one ring round the box — sem.ring.width of sem.color.focus, sem.ring.offset clear (.is-focus in the demo).
  • Disabled: the row's words and the box go to sem.color.ink-disabled, default cursor, no fade.
  • Hover: the platform's own; the kit adds none.

Usage

  • For a setting that is on or off and takes effect at once (a layer on the chart), or a yes in a form.
  • The words name the thing that is so ("Depth tints"), not an instruction ("Show depth tints").
  • The fill is ink, never the accent: a checkbox is never the view's one filled action, and never magenta.
  • One of a few, all exclusive, is a Segmented, not a column of checkboxes.

Accessibility

  • A real checkbox inside its <label>: the words name it and are part of the target, so the row is touch tall even though the box is 18.
  • Space toggles it; the platform announces checked and unchecked.
  • Disabled words in ink-disabled are below the words' floor on purpose: they are not there to be read.
components/checkbox/component.css
/* Checkbox — ui/Checkbox.tsx (checkboxStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes
 * --sem-* only.
 *
 * The platform's own box and tick, inked in the kit's inverse, and the words
 * beside it part of the target: the whole row is a <label>, never shorter
 * than a thumb.
 *
 * `.is-focus` holds the ring still for the catalog; the product reaches the
 * same rule through :focus-visible. */

.wf-checkbox {
  display: inline-flex;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  min-height: var(--sem-size-touch);
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x2);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-body);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-prose);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-prose);
  cursor: pointer;
}
.wf-checkbox:has(:disabled) {
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-disabled);
  cursor: default;
}

/* The tick is what says checked, so the fill under it is the kit's ink and
 * not the accent: a checkbox is never the one filled action. */
.wf-checkbox__input {
  width: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 4.5);
  height: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 4.5);
  flex-shrink: 0;
  margin: 0;
  accent-color: var(--sem-color-inverse);
}
.wf-checkbox__input:not(:disabled):focus-visible,
.wf-checkbox__input.is-focus {
  outline: var(--sem-ring-width) solid var(--sem-color-focus);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-ring-offset);
}
.wf-checkbox__input:disabled {
  cursor: default;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-disabled);
  opacity: 1;
}

.wf-checkbox__label {
  min-width: 0;
}

Chip

Chip

Chip · night chart (proposed)

Gear 6 m Sold Galway

glass

Cover Photos: 4

A label on a thing: a category, a condition, a status (ui/Chip.tsx, chipStyles). A tag in the figures' face, in a capsule ruled with a hairline. It labels; it is never pressed.

Anatomy

  • Capsule: .wf-chip — an inline row, sem.space.x1 gap, sem.space.x0-5 by sem.space.x2-5 inset, a sem.rule.hairline border, sem.radius.full, never wrapping.
  • Words: sem.font.family.mono at sem.font.size.caption.
  • Icon: .wf-chip__icon — optional, a 10px lucide icon in currentColor (the heart of Saved, the camera of a photo count).

Variants

  • Neutral (.wf-chip, the default) — sem.color.sunken with a sem.color.line hairline, sem.color.ink-2 words. A category, a figure.
  • Warn (--warn) — sem.color.warn-ground, a sem.color.warn hairline and words: now, or degraded (Sold on a listing page, a photo that failed).
  • Glass (--glass) — paper over a photograph: an ink hairline, sem.color.glass (paper that lets a little through) with a sem.blur.glass blur behind, ink words. Goes solid (sem.color.solid, no blur) for a reader who has asked for less transparency.
  • Eyebrow (--eyebrow) — the mono label's step: sem.font.size.eyebrow, its weight and tracking, capitals. With any tone.

States

  • None. A chip is not pressed, hovered or focused; something that is pressed is a Button.

Usage

  • Glass only over a photograph (a listing's badges: Saved, Sold, the photo count, Cover). Never over the map: over the map, paper is opaque.
  • Warm means now or degraded. A chip that is only a category is neutral; do not use warm to make a tag stand out.
  • A word or a figure, never a sentence.

Accessibility

  • A plain span. A status that appears after an action (a failed upload) carries role="alert".
  • An icon is aria-hidden; give an icon-led figure a visually hidden word ("Photos: 4").
  • Ink-2 on sunken 8.9:1; warn on warn-ground 4.8:1; ink on glass reads on any picture because the paper is near solid.
components/chip/component.css
/* Chip — ui/Chip.tsx (chipStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * A tag in the figures' face: mono, in a capsule ruled with a hairline, on the
 * paper it stands on. It labels a thing (a category, a condition, a status);
 * it is never pressed. */

/* tone="neutral" (the default): the second sheet, a line-coloured hairline. */
.wf-chip {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x1);
  padding: var(--sem-space-x0-5) var(--sem-space-x2-5);
  border: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-line);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
  background: var(--sem-color-sunken);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-2);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-caption);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-caption);
  white-space: nowrap;
}

/* tone="warn": now, or degraded. A chip that is only a category is neutral. */
.wf-chip--warn {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-warn);
  background: var(--sem-color-warn-ground);
  color: var(--sem-color-warn);
}

/* tone="glass": paper over a photograph. A badge has to read on whatever the
 * picture is, so it takes the ink rule and paper that lets a little through. */
.wf-chip--glass {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  background: var(--sem-color-glass);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(var(--sem-blur-glass));
  backdrop-filter: blur(var(--sem-blur-glass));
}

/* ...and goes solid for a reader who has declined transparency. */
@media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce) {
  .wf-chip--glass {
    background: var(--sem-color-solid);
    -webkit-backdrop-filter: none;
    backdrop-filter: none;
  }
}

/* eyebrow: the mono label's step, in tracked capitals. */
.wf-chip--eyebrow {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-eyebrow);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-eyebrow);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-eyebrow);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-eyebrow);
  text-transform: uppercase;
}

/* A 10px lucide icon in currentColor beside the words (Saved, a photo count). */
.wf-chip__icon {
  width: var(--sem-space-x2-5);
  height: var(--sem-space-x2-5);
  flex-shrink: 0;
}

4 unread 12 unread 99+ unread

A number in a badge (ui/Count.tsx, countStyles), drawn as the chart draws a spot's light: a figure in a ring.

Anatomy

  • Ring: .wf-count — sem.space.x5 tall and at least as wide, sem.space.x1 either side, a sem.rule.hairline ink border, a full capsule (sem.radius.full).
  • Figure: sem.font.family.mono at sem.font.size.caption, line-height 1, sem.font.weight.semibold, tabular digits.
  • Label: .wf-count__label — optional, visually hidden: what is counted, so a screen reader hears "4 unread".

Variants

  • Strong (.wf-count, the default) — filled in sem.color.inverse, sem.color.ink-inverse figure: unread, loud.
  • Quiet (--quiet) — sem.color.card with an ink figure: a tally, or unread below the threshold that makes it loud.

States

  • Zero: nothing is drawn.
  • Over 99: "99+". Past that the number stops being read, so it stops being counted.

Usage

  • Beside the thing counted: a channel in the rail, the bell.
  • Strong is said in fill and weight together, so it survives greyscale; do not colour a count.
  • Never magenta, never warm: a count is not the best of anything, and not degraded.

Accessibility

  • With a label, the badge reads as "4 unread". Without one it is aria-hidden, for a control whose own label already says the number.
  • Paper on ink 14.6:1; ink on paper 14.6:1.
components/count/component.css
/* Count — ui/Count.tsx (countStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * A number in a badge, drawn as the chart draws a spot's light: a figure in a
 * ring. Unread is said in fill and weight together, never colour alone. Past
 * 99 the number stops being read, so it stops being counted ("99+"). Nothing
 * is drawn for zero. */

/* tone="strong" (the default): filled in ink. */
.wf-count {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  display: inline-grid;
  place-items: center;
  height: var(--sem-space-x5);
  min-width: var(--sem-space-x5);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-x1);
  border: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
  background: var(--sem-color-inverse);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-inverse);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-caption);
  line-height: 1;
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}

/* tone="quiet": ruled in ink on paper. */
.wf-count--quiet {
  background: var(--sem-color-card);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}

/* What is counted, for a screen reader only ("4 unread"). */
.wf-count__label {
  position: absolute;
  width: 1px;
  height: 1px;
  padding: 0;
  margin: -1px;
  overflow: hidden;
  clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
  white-space: nowrap;
  border-width: 0;
}

The chart's box as a modal (ui/Dialog.tsx, dialogStyles), and the question with one destructive answer built on it (ui/ConfirmDialog.tsx). A native dialog, so focus is trapped, Escape cancels and the page behind is inert. Its buttons are the Button component's classes.

Anatomy

  • Box: .wf-dialog — 11/12 of the width up to sem.container.dialog, sem.space.x7 inset (sem.space.x5 under sem.breakpoint.wide), a grid with sem.space.x5 between its parts. Paper (sem.color.card with sem.texture.grain) in the double rule: a sem.rule.hairline ink border plus sem.shadow.frame, then sem.shadow.surface. Square (sem.radius.dialog). Sentences in sem.font.family.body.
  • Backdrop: ::backdrop in sem.color.scrim, a wash of paper, over a sem.blur.scrim blur of the page or the map behind; it fades in with sem.animate.scrim-in. Where the browser cannot blur, or the reader asks for less transparency, it is sem.color.scrim-solid with no blur. The product's one recipe for it is ui/Backdrop.tsx (scrim, Backdrop).
  • Head: .wf-dialog__head — the title and the close button, top-aligned and sem.space.x3 apart, over a hairline ink rule with sem.space.x3 beneath.
  • Title: .wf-dialog__title — the display face at sem.font.size.lead and sem.font.weight.lead, in ink.
  • Close: an icon button, quiet and small (.wf-button--icon.wf-button--sm), aria-label="Close", a 15px X.
  • Body: .wf-dialog__body — a grid, sem.space.x3 gaps, sem.font.size.prose in sem.color.ink-2.
  • Actions: .wf-dialog__actions — a wrapping row set right, sem.space.x2 apart. The filled action, if any, comes last.

Variants

  • Md (the default) — up to sem.container.dialog (420px).
  • Wide (--wide) — up to sem.container.dialog-wide (640px), for a form or a table.
  • Dismissible (the default) — draws the close button. A question with its own Cancel does without it.
  • ConfirmDialog — no close button; Cancel (.wf-button--pill) then the destructive answer (.wf-button--danger), named for what it does ("Remove listing").

States

  • Opening: sem.animate.dialog-in, a 150ms rise of sem.space.x2 from nothing; none for a reader who asks for less motion.
  • Closed: the native dialog is hidden by the browser; the grid is set only on [open]. Any other element carrying the class is a static rendering and is drawn open.
  • Busy: work is under way that closing would orphan. Every way out is held shut: the close button and both answers are disabled, Escape and a click on the backdrop do nothing. Mark the box aria-busy="true".

Usage

  • One filled action, last in the row: the primary pill, or in a ConfirmDialog the warm danger pill, and never both.
  • Title the dialog with the question or the thing ("Remove this listing?", "Share Rusheen Bay"); keep the body to a sentence or two, figures where they can be.
  • A destructive confirmation is a dialog of its own: ConfirmDialog, not a second button in another dialog.
  • Only a press that begins and ends outside the box closes it, so a selection dragged out of a field does not throw away what was written.

Accessibility

  • dialog opened with showModal(), aria-labelledby pointing at the title. A static rendering uses role="dialog" and aria-modal="true".
  • Opening remembers what held the focus; closing hands it back (or to returnFocus when the opener has gone, a row in a closed menu).
  • In a ConfirmDialog Cancel comes first in the document, so it opens with the focus: Enter on a dialog that has just appeared is never the answer that cannot be taken back.
  • The close button carries aria-label="Close"; its icon is aria-hidden.
  • Ink on paper 14.6:1, ink-2 9.5:1; the scrim is a softening, not a contrast aid.
components/dialog/component.css
/* Dialog — ui/Dialog.tsx (dialogStyles) and ui/ConfirmDialog.tsx, rendered in
 * CSS. Consumes --sem-* only. Its buttons are the Button component's classes
 * (components/button/component.css); nothing here restyles them.
 *
 * The chart's box as a modal: paper with its grain in a double rule, the title
 * in the display face over an ink rule, the body in sentences, and a row of
 * answers with the one filled action last.
 *
 * The product draws a native <dialog>, which the browser hides with nothing
 * stronger than `display` while it is closed, so the grid is only set on
 * [open]. Any other element carrying the class (a static rendering, as in the
 * demo) is drawn open. */

.wf-dialog {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  margin: auto;
  width: 91.6667%; /* w-11/12 of what holds it */
  max-width: var(--sem-container-dialog);
  gap: var(--sem-space-x5);
  padding: var(--sem-space-x7);
  border: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-dialog);
  background-color: var(--sem-color-card);
  background-image: var(--sem-texture-grain);
  background-repeat: repeat;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-body);
  box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-frame), var(--sem-shadow-surface);
}

.wf-dialog[open],
.wf-dialog:not(dialog) {
  display: grid;
  animation: var(--sem-animate-dialog-in);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .wf-dialog[open],
  .wf-dialog:not(dialog) {
    animation: none;
  }
}

/* max-wide: under sem.breakpoint.wide (45rem) the inset narrows. */
@media (max-width: 719.98px) {
  .wf-dialog {
    padding: var(--sem-space-x5);
  }
}

/* The page behind softens under a wash of paper: the scrim, over a blur. */
.wf-dialog::backdrop {
  background: var(--sem-color-scrim);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(var(--sem-blur-scrim));
  backdrop-filter: blur(var(--sem-blur-scrim));
  animation: var(--sem-animate-scrim-in);
}
@supports not ((backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) or (-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(1px))) {
  .wf-dialog::backdrop {
    background: var(--sem-color-scrim-solid);
  }
}
@media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce) {
  .wf-dialog::backdrop {
    background: var(--sem-color-scrim-solid);
    -webkit-backdrop-filter: none;
    backdrop-filter: none;
  }
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .wf-dialog::backdrop {
    animation: none;
  }
}

/* size="wide" */
.wf-dialog--wide {
  max-width: var(--sem-container-dialog-wide);
}

/* ---- head: the title, and the close button, over an ink rule ---- */
.wf-dialog__head {
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
  padding-bottom: var(--sem-space-x3);
  border-bottom: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
}

.wf-dialog__title {
  margin: 0;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-display);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-lead);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-lead);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-lead);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}

/* ---- body: a sentence or two ---- */
.wf-dialog__body {
  display: grid;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-prose);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-prose);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-2);
}
/* The product's preflight zeroes a paragraph's margins; the gap spaces them. */
.wf-dialog__body > * {
  margin: 0;
}

/* ---- actions: the filled one, if any, last ---- */
.wf-dialog__actions {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: flex-end;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x2);
}

@keyframes dialog-in {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateY(var(--sem-space-x2));
  }
}

@keyframes scrim-in {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}

Where a list would be, when there is nothing to list (ui/Empty.tsx, emptyStyles laid over a card paneStyles). An icon in a ring, a line in the display face's italic, and what to do about it.

Anatomy

  • Container: .wf-empty — a card Pane (a sem.rule.hairline ink border, sem.color.card with sem.texture.grain, square), with a tall inset (sem.space.x14 by sem.space.x6), everything centred in a grid sem.space.x3 apart; sentences in sem.font.family.body at sem.font.size.prose, sem.color.ink-muted.
  • Icon: .wf-empty__icon — a 58px ring (a large control and a gap across, 14.5 steps), hairline, holding a 24px lucide icon in currentColor; the Image icon when none is given. Decoration, aria-hidden.
  • Title: .wf-empty__title — a p, not a heading: the display face's italic at sem.font.size.lead and sem.font.weight.lead, in ink.
  • Body: .wf-empty__body — optional; a grid up to sem.container.reading wide, centred: a sentence, and the button or link that mends it.

Variants

  • Info (the default) — the ring in ink on paper.
  • Warn (--warn) — the ring in sem.color.warn on sem.color.warn-ground, for an empty list that is empty because something failed. Only the ring goes warm; the words stay muted and the title ink.

States

  • None of its own. The action inside has the Button's states.

Usage

  • Say why it is empty in the title ("No reviews yet", "Nothing matches that search"), and what mends it in one sentence.
  • The action is a pill or a link. Use the primary pill only when it is the one filled action on the view.
  • Pick an icon that names the list (search, photo, star); do not use the warm kind to draw the eye.

Accessibility

  • The title is a paragraph, so an empty list does not add a heading to the outline; the section that holds it has its own heading.
  • The icon is decoration; a warning is said in words as well as the warm ring.
  • Muted words on paper are 5.8:1.
components/empty/component.css
/* Empty — ui/Empty.tsx (emptyStyles over paneStyles), rendered in CSS.
 * Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * Where a list would be, when there is nothing to list. It is a card Pane (one
 * ink rule, paper with its grain), restated here so the component stands on
 * its own, with a tall inset, everything centred, an icon in a ring like a
 * chart's light, and a line in the display face's italic. */

.wf-empty {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  display: grid;
  justify-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
  padding: var(--sem-space-x14) var(--sem-space-x6);
  border: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-surface);
  background-color: var(--sem-color-card);
  background-image: var(--sem-texture-grain);
  background-repeat: repeat;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-body);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-prose);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-prose);
  text-align: center;
}

/* A large control and a gap across (58px), ruled in ink like a chart's light.
 * kind="info" (the default). */
.wf-empty__icon {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 14.5);
  height: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 14.5);
  border: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
  background: var(--sem-color-card);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}

/* kind="warn": the ring goes warm, and only the ring. */
.wf-empty--warn .wf-empty__icon {
  border-color: var(--sem-color-warn);
  background: var(--sem-color-warn-ground);
  color: var(--sem-color-warn);
}

/* The display face's italic: a line, not a heading. */
.wf-empty__title {
  margin: 0;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-display);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-lead);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-lead);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-lead);
  font-style: italic;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}

/* What to do about it: a sentence, and the action that mends it. */
.wf-empty__body {
  display: grid;
  justify-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
  max-width: var(--sem-container-reading);
}
/* The product's preflight zeroes a paragraph's margins. */
.wf-empty__body > * {
  margin: 0;
}

A label, the control it names, and what is wrong with it if anything is (ui/Field.tsx, fieldStyles). The label names the thing as a chart's legend does: in tracked mono capitals.

Anatomy

  • Root: .wf-field — a grid, sem.space.x2 between label, control and message, never wider than its column (min-width: 0).
  • Label: .wf-field__label on a <label for> — IBM Plex Mono at sem.font.size.eyebrow, sem.font.weight.eyebrow, tracked sem.font.tracking.eyebrow, uppercase, sem.color.ink-muted, at sem.font.line.tight. A flex row: the words left, the hint right, on one baseline.
  • Optional hint: .wf-field__hint on a <small> inside the label — Newsreader italic at sem.font.size.body, normal weight, no tracking, sentence case, sem.color.ink-muted, set right, keeping the label's tight leading.
  • Control: any of the field controls (text input, text area, select). They share the .wf-control box owned by components/text-input/component.css; the demo links that file.
  • Optional error: .wf-field__error — Newsreader italic at sem.font.size.body in sem.color.warn, role="alert".

Variants

  • Label only; label with a hint; with an error.

States

  • Invalid: an error sets data-invalid on .wf-field, and the control inside turns warm (sem.color.warn border on sem.color.warn-ground). The rule is the control's (.wf-field[data-invalid] .wf-control, the product's group-data-invalid/field), so it lives in the text input's CSS beside the box it styles.
  • Focus, hover, disabled: the control's own; the field draws none.

Usage

  • Name the thing in a word or two: SPOT, PRICE, WING SIZE. A label never says a sentence.
  • A hint is a unit or a short rule ("whole euro", "m²"), not instructions.
  • An error says what to do, briefly ("Write it as 6.5"). Wrong is said in words as well as warm, never colour alone.
  • Fields in a form sit in sem.grid.fields columns.

Accessibility

  • The <label for> names the control, and taking it focuses the control.
  • The hint is inside the label, so it is read with the name.
  • The error carries role="alert", so it is announced when it appears; tie it to the control with aria-describedby and set aria-invalid="true" on the control.
  • Label and hint are ink-muted, 5.8:1 on paper; the error is warn, 5.7:1 on paper.
components/field/component.css
/* Field — ui/Field.tsx (fieldStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * A label, the control it names, and what is wrong with it if anything is.
 * The label is the mono label, as a chart's legend names a thing (TITLE,
 * PRICE); a hint beside it on the same line goes back to the body face's
 * italic. `data-invalid` on the field turns the control inside warm: that
 * rule lives with the control, in ../text-input/component.css
 * (`.wf-field[data-invalid] .wf-control`), as the product's group/field. */

.wf-field {
  display: grid;
  min-width: 0;
  align-content: start;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x2);
}

/* The mono label at a label's leading (tight), not a paragraph's. */
.wf-field__label {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x2);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-eyebrow);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-tight);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-eyebrow);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-eyebrow);
  text-transform: uppercase;
}

/* The hint: sentence case in the body face's italic, set right on the
 * label's line and keeping its leading. */
.wf-field__hint {
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-body);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-tight);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-normal);
  font-style: italic;
  letter-spacing: 0;
  text-align: right;
  text-transform: none;
}

/* What is wrong, in words, in warm italic. */
.wf-field__error {
  color: var(--sem-color-warn);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-body);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-body);
  font-style: italic;
}

Figure

Figure · night chart (proposed)

12kn 1422kn 1326 18kn

A number first and large, in the mono face's tabular digits (ui/Figure.tsx, figureStyles), its unit small after it and, where there is one, a second figure raised after it the way the chart writes a gust over the mean (14 g22 is 14²²).

Anatomy

  • Root: .wf-figure — an inline flex row on the baseline, sem.space.x0-5 apart, sem.font.family.mono, tabular, never wrapping, in sem.color.ink.
  • Value: .wf-figure__value — the number.
  • Sup: .wf-figure__sup — the raised figure, set to the top of the row, at the caption step in sem.font.weight.medium, sem.color.ink-muted.
  • Unit: .wf-figure__unit — kn, m, €, %, at the caption step in sem.color.ink-muted.

Variants

  • --sm — the value at sem.font.size.body, semibold: a row's small figure.
  • md (the default) — the figure step (sem.font.size.figure, its line, weight and tracking): the number a row is about.
  • --lg — the reading, sem.font.size.reading, semibold: the wind speed, one a view.
  • --alarm — the raised figure is the one to watch (a gust well over the mean): semibold, in sem.color.pen-ink.

States

  • None; it is not interactive.

Usage

  • Say it as a figure, not a sentence: 14 g22 · WSW · 6 m.
  • Figures are never in the body face; sentences never in this one.
  • --lg once a view. --alarm is a gust, not emphasis.

Accessibility

  • Where the digits alone do not say what the figure is, give the root role="img" and an aria-label ("14 knots gusting 22").
  • The alarm is heavier as well as red, so it survives greyscale; pen-ink is 4.9:1 on paper.
components/figure/component.css
/* Figure — ui/Figure.tsx (figureStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * The number first and large in the mono face's tabular digits, its unit
 * small after it and, where there is one, a second figure raised after it the
 * way the chart writes a gust over the mean (14 g22 -> 14²²). */

.wf-figure {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x0-5);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  white-space: nowrap;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}

/* ---- the value, by size (md, the figure step, is the default) ---- */
.wf-figure__value {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-figure);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-figure);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-figure);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-figure);
}
.wf-figure--sm .wf-figure__value {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-body);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
  letter-spacing: inherit;
}
/* The reading: one a view, the wind speed. */
.wf-figure--lg .wf-figure__value {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-reading);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-reading);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
  letter-spacing: inherit;
}

/* ---- the raised figure: the gust over the mean ---- */
.wf-figure__sup {
  align-self: flex-start;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-caption);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-caption);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
}
/* The one to watch: a gust well over the mean, in the pen's ink and heavier. */
.wf-figure--alarm .wf-figure__sup {
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
  color: var(--sem-color-pen-ink);
}

/* ---- the unit: kn, m, €, % ---- */
.wf-figure__unit {
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-caption);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-caption);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
}

Headline

Headline

Headline · 44 from 720, title · 30 under it

Donabate: a three-star Friday morning on a 5.5 m

Under 720 (held) · the title step

Donabate: a three-star Friday morning on a 5.5 m

Without a mark

How the stars work

Headline · night chart (proposed)

Donabate: a three-star Friday morning on a 5.5 m

One a page, on a page that is read, saying the verdict in a line (ui/Headline.tsx, headlineStyles): "Donabate: a three-star Friday morning on a 5.5 m".

Anatomy

  • Base: .wf-headline — an h1 (or h2), no margin, sem.font.family.display at the headline step (sem.font.size.headline, its line, sem.font.weight.headline, sem.font.tracking.headline), Fraunces held at its display cut ("opsz" 144), balanced, in sem.color.ink.
  • Soft: .wf-headline__soft — an em for the soft tail of the line, in sem.font.weight.normal italic, still set tight.
  • Mark: .wf-headline__mark — a span for the colon after a name, in sem.color.chart-magenta.

Variants

  • From 720px (sem.breakpoint.wide) the headline step (44); under it, the title step (30, its line, weight and tracking). .is-narrow holds the phone step for the catalog; the product reaches it through the media query only.
  • With or without the mark: a page about a place has the colon; "How the stars work" does not.

States

  • None; it is not interactive.

Usage

  • One a page, and only on a page that is read. A page without one heads itself with a SectionHeading --title.
  • Say the verdict in a line; the soft tail carries what qualifies it.
  • The magenta mark is that page's one "best of"; do not use magenta again in the headline.

Accessibility

  • The page's h1. The soft tail is an em, which is what it means.
  • Ink on paper 14.6:1; the magenta colon 5.7:1, and it carries no meaning alone.
components/headline/component.css
/* Headline — ui/Headline.tsx (headlineStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * One a page, on a page that is read, saying the verdict in a line: Fraunces
 * at its display cut (opsz 144), heavy and tight, the soft part of the line in
 * its light italic, and a mark in the chart's magenta (the colon after a
 * name). It steps to the title under 720px.
 *
 * `.is-narrow` holds the phone step still for the catalog; the product reaches
 * the same rule through the media query alone. */

.wf-headline {
  margin: 0;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-display);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-headline);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-headline);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-headline);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-headline);
  font-variation-settings: "opsz" 144;
  text-wrap: balance;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}

/* max-wide: under sem.breakpoint.wide (45rem), the title step. */
@media (max-width: 719.98px) {
  .wf-headline {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-title);
    line-height: var(--sem-font-line-title);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-title);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-title);
  }
}
.wf-headline.is-narrow {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-title);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-title);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-title);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-title);
}

/* The soft tail: light italic, still set tight (tracking-tight on display type). */
.wf-headline__soft {
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-normal);
  font-style: italic;
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-headline);
}

/* The mark: the colon after a name, in the chart's magenta. */
.wf-headline__mark {
  color: var(--sem-color-chart-magenta);
}

Hour cell

Hour cell

Eight hours of the dock · past, now and selected, dark, a new day

Mon5 Tue6
16 17Mon 17:00 18 19 20 07 08 09
Stars
Windkn 13g21 12g20 11g18 10g17 8g15 8g14 8g14 7g14
From WSW WSW WSW WSW WSW N N N
Wingm² 6 6.5 7 7.5 8 8

Hour cell · night chart (proposed)

Mon5 Tue6
16 17Mon 17:00 18 19 20 07 08 09
Stars
Windkn 13g21 12g20 11g18 10g17 8g15 8g14 8g14 7g14
From WSW WSW WSW WSW WSW N N N
Wingm² 6 6.5 7 7.5 8 8

One hour's column of the dock's table: the hour, its stars, the wind, where it comes from against the beach, and the wing to take. The mockup's table.tt (design/chart/1-the-chart.html); no ui/ primitive yet.

Anatomy

  • Dock: .wf-hour-cell__dock, the strip that scrolls sideways (no visible scrollbar), a region with a label and tabindex="0" so a keyboard can scroll it; its focus ring is drawn inside.
  • Table: .wf-hour-cell__table, a real <table>, collapsed, fixed layout, mono with tabular digits. A <colgroup> sets the row-label column (__col-label, 64px) and one <col> per hour: 52px on a phone, 62px from sem.breakpoint.wide.
  • Row labels: .wf-hour-cell__label, a <th scope="row"> in the mono label (eyebrow, tracked capitals, ink-muted) that stays put while the hours scroll; a unit beside it in lower case, __unit ("kn", "m²").
  • Rows, each .wf-hour-cell__row with a modifier:
  • --day: the day's head, "Mon 5" (the day in the display face at body, the date small), a hairline under it.
  • --hour: the hour, "17", at caption semibold, an ink rule under the row; these cells are <th scope="col">.
  • --stars: __stars, the hour's five places drawn with the chart's STAR path as ui/StarGlyphs draws it, 9.5px a star (8.6 on a phone): __star solid, __star--faded an outline at sem.opacity.faded (what the wind alone gives), __star--dot at sem.opacity.dot for each not reached.
  • --wind: .wf-wind-figure--cell, "14 g22".
  • --from: __from, the downwind arrow (12px), the compass point, and the shore-wind glyph (.wf-shore-compass--wind --sm).
  • --wing: the wing in m², body semibold.
  • Cell: .wf-hour-cell, centred, 20px tall (the hour row 18).

Variants

  • None: one column is one hour. Its state is a set of classes repeated on every cell of the column.

States

  • Selected (--sel): the column on sem.color.sunken; the hour cell filled in ink with paper figures, and aria-current="time" on it.
  • Night (--night): the hatch (sem.color.hatch, 135°), the hour in ink-muted at normal weight, no stars and no wing. The wind is still shown.
  • Past (--past): the column at sem.opacity.past.
  • First hour of a day (--day-start): a sem.rule.heavy ink rule on its left, through the day's head and every row.
  • Now (--now): the present-hour cursor, a sem.rule.heavy line of sem.color.pen at sem.opacity.pen down the middle of the column, run up through the day's head, with __flag at its top: "Mon 17:00" in mono semibold at caption, paper words (sem.color.ink-inverse) on the pen. The flag sits in the hour's header cell. In the dock the cursor stays in the middle and the hours scroll under it, so the selected hour is the cursor's.
  • Hover: a cell not selected goes to sem.color.sunken.

Usage

  • Load components/wind-figure/component.css and components/shore-compass/component.css beside this one.
  • The dock's day runs 07 to 20; a dark hour is never left blank and never rated.
  • The cursor and the "Best" loop are the dock's pen marks: no other pen on the strip but the shore glyph's offshore arrow.
  • Keep the row labels to a word and a unit: STARS, WIND kn, FROM, WING m².

Accessibility

  • A real table: hours are column headers (<th scope="col">), the row labels row headers (<th scope="row">), so a screen reader announces "17, Wind, 12 knots gusting 20".
  • The stars carry role="img" with "3 of 5 stars, 4 on the wind alone"; a dark hour has no stars to read, and its hour is still announced.
  • The selected hour is aria-current="time". The flag is aria-hidden: the time it shows is already the column's header and the day's head.
  • The flag is set on the pen's handwriting ink (sem.color.pen-ink), where paper reads at 4.9:1; on the stroke red (sem.color.pen) it would be 4.1:1, below 4.5:1 for small text. The line itself stays in sem.color.pen. The selected hour also differs in fill, not in colour alone.
  • The strip scrolls with arrow keys once focused; the focus ring is drawn inside its edge.
components/hour-cell/component.css
/* Hour cell — one hour's column of the dock's table: the mockup's `table.tt`
 * (design/chart/1-the-chart.html). No ui/ primitive yet; drawn as the
 * signed-off mockup draws it. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * The table is a real <table>: a row of hours (column headers), then STARS,
 * WIND kn, FROM and WING m², each headed by a mono label. An hour is the
 * column of cells that share its state classes:
 *   --sel        the selected hour: the column on the second sheet, its hour
 *                filled in ink with paper figures.
 *   --night      a dark hour: hatched, its hour faint and light, no stars.
 *   --past       gone: the column at the past opacity.
 *   --day-start  the first hour of a day: a heavier ink rule on its left.
 *   --now        the present-hour cursor: a line of the pen down the column,
 *                and a flag at its head (`__flag`, in the hour's header cell).
 *
 * The wind and its gust are `.wf-wind-figure--cell`, the shore glyph is
 * `.wf-shore-compass--wind`; load those components' CSS beside this one.
 * The star is drawn statically with the chart's STAR path, as ui/StarGlyphs
 * draws it: solid, faded (the wind alone), a dot for each it does not reach. */

/* The strip scrolls sideways under the fixed row labels. */
.wf-hour-cell__dock {
  position: relative;
  max-width: 100%;
  overflow-x: auto;
  overflow-y: hidden;
  scrollbar-width: none;
  overscroll-behavior-x: contain;
  /* Room above the hours for the cursor's flag. */
  padding-top: var(--sem-space-x1);
}
.wf-hour-cell__dock::-webkit-scrollbar {
  display: none;
}
.wf-hour-cell__dock:focus-visible {
  outline: var(--sem-ring-width) solid var(--sem-color-focus);
  outline-offset: calc(var(--sem-ring-offset) * -1);
}

.wf-hour-cell__table {
  /* An hour's width: 52 on a phone, 62 from sem.breakpoint.wide. */
  --wf-hour-cell-w: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 13);
  width: max-content;
  border-collapse: collapse;
  table-layout: fixed;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
@media (min-width: 720px) {
  /* sem.breakpoint.wide */
  .wf-hour-cell__table {
    --wf-hour-cell-w: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 15.5);
  }
}
.wf-hour-cell__table col {
  width: var(--wf-hour-cell-w);
}
.wf-hour-cell__table col.wf-hour-cell__col-label {
  width: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 16);
}

/* ---- the row labels: the mono label, a unit beside it in lower case ---- */
.wf-hour-cell__label {
  position: sticky;
  left: 0;
  z-index: 4;
  padding: 0;
  background-color: var(--sem-color-ground);
  background-image: var(--sem-texture-grain);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-eyebrow);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-eyebrow);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-eyebrow);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-eyebrow);
  text-align: left;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
.wf-hour-cell__unit {
  margin-left: var(--sem-space-x0-5);
  letter-spacing: 0;
  text-transform: none;
}

/* ---- a cell ---- */
.wf-hour-cell {
  position: relative;
  height: var(--sem-space-x5);
  padding: 0;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-caption);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-caption);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-normal);
  text-align: center;
  vertical-align: middle;
  white-space: nowrap;
  cursor: pointer;
}

/* The day's head: its name in the display face, the date small. */
.wf-hour-cell__row--day .wf-hour-cell {
  height: var(--sem-space-x5);
  border-bottom: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-line);
  text-align: left;
  cursor: default;
}
.wf-hour-cell__day {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x1);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-x1-5);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-caption);
}
.wf-hour-cell__day b {
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-display);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
}

/* The hour: 11px semibold, an ink rule under the row. */
.wf-hour-cell__row--hour .wf-hour-cell {
  height: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 4.5);
  border-bottom: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
}
.wf-hour-cell__row--wing .wf-hour-cell {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-body);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
}

/* ---- the stars, as ui/StarGlyphs draws them, at 9.5px a star ---- */
.wf-hour-cell__stars {
  display: block;
  margin: 0 auto;
  overflow: visible;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}
@media (max-width: 719.98px) {
  /* sem.breakpoint.wide: a phone's 52px hour holds the five at 8.6px. */
  .wf-hour-cell__stars {
    width: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 11.5);
    height: auto;
  }
}
.wf-hour-cell__star {
  fill: currentColor;
}
.wf-hour-cell__star--faded {
  fill: none;
  stroke: currentColor;
  opacity: var(--sem-opacity-faded);
}
.wf-hour-cell__star--dot {
  fill: currentColor;
  opacity: var(--sem-opacity-dot);
}

/* ---- FROM: the downwind arrow, the point, the shore glyph ---- */
.wf-hour-cell__from {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
}
.wf-hour-cell__from .wf-wind-figure__arrow {
  width: var(--sem-space-x3);
  height: var(--sem-space-x3);
}
.wf-hour-cell__from .wf-wind-figure__point {
  margin: 0 var(--sem-space-x0-5) 0 0;
}

/* ---- states of the column ---- */
.wf-hour-cell--day-start {
  border-left: var(--sem-rule-heavy) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
}
.wf-hour-cell--night {
  background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sem-color-hatch) 0 1px, transparent 1px 4px);
}
.wf-hour-cell__row--hour .wf-hour-cell--night {
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-normal);
}
.wf-hour-cell--past {
  opacity: var(--sem-opacity-past);
}
.wf-hour-cell--sel {
  background-color: var(--sem-color-sunken);
}
.wf-hour-cell__row--hour .wf-hour-cell--sel {
  background-color: var(--sem-color-inverse);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-inverse);
}
.wf-hour-cell:not(.wf-hour-cell--sel):hover {
  background-color: var(--sem-color-sunken);
}

/* The present-hour cursor: the pen's line down the middle of the column. */
.wf-hour-cell--now::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  bottom: calc(var(--sem-rule-hairline) * -1);
  left: 50%;
  z-index: 3;
  border-left: var(--sem-rule-heavy) solid var(--sem-color-pen);
  opacity: var(--sem-opacity-pen);
  pointer-events: none;
}
/* From the hour's cell it runs up through the day's head to the flag. */
.wf-hour-cell__row--hour .wf-hour-cell--now::after {
  top: calc(var(--sem-space-x5) * -1);
}
/* The flag: the hour in the pen, in paper words, at the cursor's head. */
.wf-hour-cell__flag {
  position: absolute;
  bottom: 100%;
  left: calc(50% + var(--sem-space-x1));
  z-index: 3;
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-x1);
  background: var(--sem-color-pen-ink);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-inverse);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-caption);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-caption);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
  white-space: nowrap;
  pointer-events: none;
}

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <title>Hour cell — wingfoil-chart</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="../../foundations/tokens.css" />
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="../wind-figure/component.css" />
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="../shore-compass/component.css" />
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="component.css" />
    <style>
      /* Demo scaffolding only: the paper, a mono label per row, and rows. */
      body {
        margin: 0;
      }
      .demo {
        padding: var(--sem-space-x5);
        background-color: var(--sem-color-ground);
        background-image: var(--sem-texture-grain);
        color: var(--sem-color-ink);
        font-family: var(--sem-font-family-body);
        font-size: var(--sem-font-size-prose);
        line-height: var(--sem-font-line-prose);
      }
      .demo + .demo {
        border-top: var(--sem-rule-double) double var(--sem-color-ink);
      }
      .demo__head {
        margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-x3);
        padding-bottom: var(--sem-space-x1);
        border-bottom: var(--sem-rule-heavy) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
        font-family: var(--sem-font-family-display);
        font-size: var(--sem-font-size-lead);
        line-height: var(--sem-font-line-lead);
        font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-lead);
      }
      .demo__label {
        margin: var(--sem-space-x4) 0 var(--sem-space-x2);
        font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
        font-size: var(--sem-font-size-eyebrow);
        line-height: var(--sem-font-line-eyebrow);
        font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-eyebrow);
        letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-eyebrow);
        text-transform: uppercase;
        color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
      }
      .demo__row {
        display: flex;
        flex-wrap: wrap;
        align-items: center;
        gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
      }
      .demo__map {
        padding: var(--sem-space-x3);
        background: var(--sem-color-sea-3);
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <section class="demo" data-mode="light">
      <h2 class="demo__head">Hour cell</h2>

      <p class="demo__label">Eight hours of the dock · past, now and selected, dark, a new day</p>

The mono label as an element (ui/Kicker.tsx, kickerStyles; MONO_LABEL in ui/tv.ts is the same classes): tracked capitals in IBM Plex Mono, as a chart names its parts and a broadsheet heads its columns.

Anatomy

  • .wf-kicker — no margin, sem.font.family.mono at the eyebrow step (sem.font.size.eyebrow, its line, sem.font.weight.eyebrow, tracked sem.font.tracking.eyebrow), uppercase.

Variants

  • Muted (the default) — sem.color.ink-muted: a label over a figure, a column head.
  • --ink — sem.color.ink: a label that heads something.
  • --pen — sem.color.pen-ink: the label of the one thing that matters ("Best of the week"), beside the pen's mark.

States

  • None; it is never pressed.

Usage

  • Names a thing in a word or two, and never says a sentence: STARS, WIND KN, BEST MON, LOW TIDE.
  • A figure leads and the kicker names it, above or beside.
  • A paragraph by default; a span in a row; a heading where it is one.
  • The eyebrow step (10px) is the floor, and it is for this label only.

Accessibility

  • Write the words in sentence or title case; the capitals are CSS, so a screen reader does not spell them out.
  • Muted is 5.8:1 on paper (5.4:1 on sunken); pen-ink 4.9:1.
components/kicker/component.css
/* Kicker — ui/Kicker.tsx (kickerStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * The mono label (MONO_LABEL in ui/tv.ts): tracked capitals in IBM Plex Mono
 * at the eyebrow step, as a chart names its parts and a broadsheet heads its
 * columns. STARS · WIND KN · BEST MON. A word or two; never a sentence. */

.wf-kicker {
  margin: 0;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-eyebrow);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-eyebrow);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-eyebrow);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-eyebrow);
  text-transform: uppercase;
  /* tone muted, the default */
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
}

/* ---- tones ---- */
.wf-kicker--ink {
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}
/* The pen's ink, for the label of the one thing that matters. */
.wf-kicker--pen {
  color: var(--sem-color-pen-ink);
}

Link

Link · night chart (proposed)

Low tide 13:25 · 1.7 m; the tide table has the week, and Rusheen Bay the best of it.

Dollymount Donabate

A link in text (ui/Link.tsx, linkStyles): a plain <a href> in the quiet ink, underlined in running text, magenta under the pointer.

Anatomy

  • Link: .wf-link on an <a href> — the surrounding face and size, in sem.color.quiet, sem.radius.control so the focus ring sits square but for the field's 2px.
  • Underline (the default): a sem.rule.hairline line in sem.color.line-strong, 3px under the words.

Variants

  • Underlined (the default) — in running text, where ink alone does not say "link".
  • Plain (.wf-link--plain) — no underline, for a list of nothing but links: a footer, a menu, a row of spot names.

States

  • Hover: the words go to sem.color.chart-magenta, and the underline with them (currentColor); .is-hover holds it in the demo. The link under the pointer is one of magenta's few uses.
  • Focus: :focus-visible draws the one ring — sem.ring.width of sem.color.focus, sem.ring.offset clear (.is-focus in the demo).
  • Visited: no look of its own.

Usage

  • Underlined wherever a link sits among other words; plain only where every item is a link.
  • The words say where it goes ("tide table", "Rusheen Bay"), never "here".
  • A way back or on in the label face ("← Chart") is a Button --link, not this.
  • In the product a section's router takes the link over with its own click handler; it still opens in a new tab when asked to.

Accessibility

  • A real <a href>: announced as a link, followed with Enter, and openable in a new tab.
  • The underline means a link is not said by colour alone in text; a plain link relies on its place in a list of links.
  • Contrast: quiet ink 14.6:1 on paper, magenta 5.7:1; the underline's line-strong is a stroke, 3.7:1.
components/link/component.css
/* Link — ui/Link.tsx (linkStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * A link in text. In running text it is underlined, because ink alone does
 * not say "link": a hairline in the stroke grey under the quiet ink, and both
 * go to the chart's magenta under the pointer. In a list of nothing but links
 * (a footer, a menu) it can go plain.
 *
 * `.is-hover` and `.is-focus` hold a state still for the catalog; the product
 * reaches the same rules through :hover and :focus-visible. */

.wf-link {
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  color: var(--sem-color-quiet);
  text-decoration: underline;
  text-decoration-thickness: var(--sem-rule-hairline);
  text-decoration-color: var(--sem-color-line-strong);
  /* underline-offset-3 is Tailwind's 3px, not a spacing step; no token holds
   * an underline offset (recorded as a gap). */
  text-underline-offset: 3px;
  transition-property: color, background-color, border-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color;
  transition-duration: var(--sem-duration-fast);
}

.wf-link:hover,
.wf-link.is-hover {
  color: var(--sem-color-chart-magenta);
  text-decoration-color: currentColor;
}

/* The one ring: 2px of the chart's magenta, 2px clear (RING). */
.wf-link:focus-visible,
.wf-link.is-focus {
  outline: var(--sem-ring-width) solid var(--sem-color-focus);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-ring-offset);
}

/* ---- plain: in a list of nothing but links, no underline ---- */
.wf-link--plain {
  text-decoration: none;
}
