The header every page that is read shares (ui/Masthead.tsx, mastheadStyles, MastheadMark): the site menu, the nameplate with its section in the mono label, and the section's few actions set right, over the broadsheet's double rule.

Anatomy

  • Root: .wf-masthead — a sticky header at the top, at sem.z-index.header, on sem.color.ground with sem.texture.grain, its top padding sem.space.x2 or the notch's inset, whichever is larger.
  • Bar: .wf-masthead__bar — a flex row at least sem.space.x14 tall, sem.space.x3 gaps, sem.space.x2 under, the sem.rule.double ink rule along its foot only.
  • Menu: the site menu's trigger, a Button --raised --icon --sm (the square instrument) with an aria-label.
  • Brand: .wf-masthead__brand — the caller's link, holding a Wordmark --md with .wf-masthead__mark and, where the page is not the map's own, the section.
  • Section: .wf-masthead__section — the mono label in sem.color.ink-muted after a sem.rule.hairline in sem.color.line, sem.space.x3 clear of it: MARKET, COMMUNITY.
  • Actions: .wf-masthead__actions — set right, sem.space.x2 apart: the one filled action, Sign in.

Variants

  • From 720px (sem.breakpoint.wide) the name and the section sit side by side.
  • Under 720px the section stands under the name with no hairline, the wordmark steps to sem.font.size.lead, the bar's gaps close to sem.space.x2 and the actions' to sem.space.x1, so the menu, the name and two actions share 390px. .is-narrow on the root holds this layout at any width for the catalog; the product reaches it through the media query only.

States

  • Focus: the brand link draws the one ring, sem.ring.width of sem.color.focus, sem.ring.offset clear, round its sem.radius.control corners (.is-focus holds it in the demo).
  • The menu and actions keep their Button states.
  • The demo holds the masthead in place (position: static), as the product's own gallery does; on a page it sticks to the top.

Usage

  • Every page that is read starts with it: market, community, the spot page. The map has its own head and does not use it.
  • The brand link is the section's own, because each router takes a link over in its own way; the classes and the mark inside it are these.
  • One filled action at most in the actions, usually none.
  • Load the Button and Wordmark CSS beside it.

Accessibility

  • A header landmark; the actions in a nav with its own aria-label ("Marketplace").
  • The brand link carries an aria-label naming where it goes ("wingfoil.ie Market, home"); the menu button an aria-label ("Site menu").
  • The section label is sem.color.ink-muted, 5.8:1 on paper.
components/masthead/component.css
/* Masthead — ui/Masthead.tsx (mastheadStyles, MastheadMark), rendered in CSS.
 * Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * The masthead every page that is read shares: the site menu (a raised icon
 * Button), the brand link holding the Wordmark and the section after a
 * hairline in the mono label, and the section's few actions set right, all
 * over the broadsheet's double rule. Paper with its grain, sticky, inside the
 * page measure as a nameplate sits inside the type area.
 *
 * On a phone (under sem.breakpoint.wide, 45rem) the section stands under the
 * name, the wordmark steps to lead and the gaps close, so the menu, the name
 * and two actions share 390px. `.is-narrow` on the masthead holds that layout
 * still for the catalog; the product reaches it through the media query only.
 * `.is-focus` holds the brand link's ring, as `:focus-visible` draws it. */

.wf-masthead {
  position: sticky;
  top: 0;
  z-index: var(--sem-z-index-header);
  /* pt-safe-2: the step, or the notch's inset, whichever is the larger. */
  padding-top: max(var(--sem-space-x2), env(safe-area-inset-top));
  background-color: var(--sem-color-ground);
  background-image: var(--sem-texture-grain);
  background-repeat: repeat;
}

/* The double rule along the foot only: the other three sides go to zero first. */
.wf-masthead__bar {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
  min-height: var(--sem-space-x14);
  padding-bottom: var(--sem-space-x2);
  border: 0 solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  border-bottom: var(--sem-rule-double) double var(--sem-color-ink);
}

/* The brand link: the wordmark, then the section. */
.wf-masthead__brand {
  display: inline-flex;
  min-width: 0;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  text-decoration: none;
}
.wf-masthead__brand:focus-visible,
.wf-masthead__brand.is-focus {
  outline: var(--sem-ring-width) solid var(--sem-color-focus);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-ring-offset);
}

/* The section, after a hairline: MARKET, COMMUNITY. */
.wf-masthead__section {
  padding-left: var(--sem-space-x3);
  border: 0 solid var(--sem-color-line);
  border-left-width: var(--sem-rule-hairline);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-eyebrow);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-eyebrow);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-eyebrow);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-eyebrow);
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
}

/* The section's own actions, set right. */
.wf-masthead__actions {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x2);
  margin-left: auto;
}

/* ---- the phone: max-wide, under sem.breakpoint.wide (45rem) ---- */
@media (max-width: 719.98px) {
  .wf-masthead__bar {
    gap: var(--sem-space-x2);
  }
  .wf-masthead__brand {
    flex-direction: column;
    align-items: flex-start;
    gap: var(--sem-space-x0-5);
  }
  /* The wordmark steps down to lead. */
  .wf-masthead__brand .wf-masthead__mark {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-lead);
  }
  .wf-masthead__section {
    padding-left: 0;
    border-left-width: 0;
  }
  .wf-masthead__actions {
    gap: var(--sem-space-x1);
  }
}

/* The same phone layout, held for the catalog at any width. */
.wf-masthead.is-narrow .wf-masthead__bar {
  gap: var(--sem-space-x2);
}
.wf-masthead.is-narrow .wf-masthead__brand {
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: flex-start;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x0-5);
}
.wf-masthead.is-narrow .wf-masthead__brand .wf-masthead__mark {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-lead);
}
.wf-masthead.is-narrow .wf-masthead__section {
  padding-left: 0;
  border-left-width: 0;
}
.wf-masthead.is-narrow .wf-masthead__actions {
  gap: var(--sem-space-x1);
}

Notice

Notice

kind="info" · role="status"

Forecast from 13:00. Low tide 13:25 · 1.7 m.

kind="warn" · role="alert" · warm, an icon and words

Only the seller can edit this listing.

Two lines · the icon stays on the first

The forecast is six hours old. Met Éireann is not answering.

Notice · night chart (proposed)

Forecast from 13:00.
The forecast is six hours old.

Something the reader should know, said in place (ui/Notice.tsx, noticeStyles). Set off as the broadsheet sets off a note: a heavy rule down its edge. A warning interrupts.

Anatomy

  • Container: .wf-notice — a row, top-aligned, sem.space.x3 gap, sem.space.x3 by sem.space.x4 inset; a sem.rule.edge rule down the left edge and none elsewhere; sentences in sem.font.family.body at sem.font.size.prose.
  • Icon: .wf-notice__icon — a 16px lucide icon in currentColor (Info, or AlertTriangle for a warning), sem.space.x0-5 down onto the first line, never shrinking.
  • Body: .wf-notice__body — the words; free to wrap.

Variants

  • Info (.wf-notice, the default) — sem.color.sunken behind, sem.color.ink-2 words, an ink rule, the Info icon.
  • Warn (--warn) — sem.color.warn-ground behind, sem.color.warn words and rule, the triangle.

States

  • None of its own. It appears, says its piece, and is removed by whatever put it there.

Usage

  • A sentence, two at most: what happened and, where there is one, what to do.
  • Warm means degraded or an error, never "look here": a notice that is only news is info.
  • Inside a form or a panel, near what it is about, not as a toast.

Accessibility

  • Info carries role="status" (polite); warn carries role="alert", so it is read the moment it appears.
  • The warning is told three ways: colour, its own icon and its words. The icon is aria-hidden; the words carry the meaning.
  • Warn on warn-ground is 4.8:1, ink-2 on sunken 8.9:1.
components/notice/component.css
/* Notice — ui/Notice.tsx (noticeStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * Something the reader should know, said in place, and set off as the
 * broadsheet sets off a note: a heavy rule down its edge. A warning is told
 * three ways: warm, an icon of its own, and an interrupting role. */

/* kind="info" (the default): the second sheet, an ink rule. */
.wf-notice {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
  padding: var(--sem-space-x3) var(--sem-space-x4);
  border: 0;
  border-left: var(--sem-rule-edge) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  background: var(--sem-color-sunken);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-2);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-body);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-prose);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-prose);
}

/* kind="warn": degraded, an error. Warm, and nothing else is. */
.wf-notice--warn {
  border-left-color: var(--sem-color-warn);
  background: var(--sem-color-warn-ground);
  color: var(--sem-color-warn);
}

/* A 16px lucide icon in currentColor, nudged down onto the first line. */
.wf-notice__icon {
  flex-shrink: 0;
  width: var(--sem-space-x4);
  height: var(--sem-space-x4);
  margin-top: var(--sem-space-x0-5);
}

.wf-notice__body {
  min-width: 0;
}
/* The product's preflight zeroes a paragraph's margins. */
.wf-notice__body > * {
  margin: 0;
}

Pager · night chart (proposed)

Page 1 of 7

Previous and next through a long list, with the page in view between them as a figure (ui/Pager.tsx, pagerStyles). Its buttons are the Button component's small ruled pills.

Anatomy

  • Container: .wf-pager — a nav labelled "Pages", a centred row sem.space.x3 apart, sem.space.x2 above.
  • Previous: .wf-button.wf-button--pill.wf-button--sm, a 16px left chevron before its words.
  • Status: .wf-pager__status — "Page 2 of 7" in sem.font.family.mono at sem.font.size.caption, tabular, sem.color.ink-muted.
  • Next: the same pill, a 16px right chevron after its words.

Variants

  • None. One page or none to turn to draws nothing at all: an empty list is one page.

States

  • First page: Previous disabled (ink-disabled words on a line-coloured ring).
  • Last page: Next disabled.
  • Hover and focus: the pill's own (inverse under the pointer, the one magenta ring); .is-hover and .is-focus hold them in the demo.

Usage

  • Under a list of listings, threads or mentions, centred under its column.
  • Count pages from one. The status is a figure, never a sentence.
  • No filled action here: the pills stay ruled.

Accessibility

  • A nav with aria-label="Pages"; the status carries aria-current="page".
  • The chevrons are aria-hidden; the words name the buttons.
  • Disabled ends are real disabled buttons, skipped by the tab order; on a coarse pointer each pill is at least sem.size.touch tall.
components/pager/component.css
/* Pager — ui/Pager.tsx (pagerStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 * Its buttons are the Button component's classes (components/button/
 * component.css): small ruled pills, disabled at either end.
 *
 * Previous and next, and the page in view between them as a figure. Nothing at
 * all is drawn when everything fits on one page. */

.wf-pager {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
  padding-top: var(--sem-space-x2);
}

/* "Page 2 of 7": a figure, so the figures' face, small and muted. */
.wf-pager__status {
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-caption);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-caption);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
}

The box content sits in on a page that is read (ui/Pane.tsx, paneStyles). Told apart from its siblings by its rules, never its fill. Over the map the box is a Surface.

Anatomy

  • Container: .wf-pane — sem.space.x5 inset, square (sem.radius.surface), sem.color.ink words.
  • Rule: per kind (below): a hairline round it, none, or a heavy rule above.
  • Paper: sem.color.card with sem.texture.grain for a card; the second sheet (sem.color.sunken) for a well; nothing for a ruled section.
  • Content is free: the Pane sets no face or size of its own.

Variants

  • Card (.wf-pane, kind="card", the default) — a sem.rule.hairline ink border, paper with its grain.
  • Sunken (--sunken) — sem.color.sunken, no rule: a well, an aside, a breakdown of figures.
  • Ruled (--ruled) — a sem.rule.heavy ink rule above, nothing at the sides, no fill; inset sem.space.x3 above and none at the sides or foot, so it lines up with its column. Most of a page is this.
  • Double (--double) — adds sem.shadow.frame, the chart's box, for the one pane that matters.
  • Standing (--standing) — a pane on its own rather than in a column: sem.shadow.surface and a sem.space.x6 inset from sem.breakpoint.wide (720px) up, sem.space.x5 under it. With --double both shadows draw, the frame first.

States

  • None of its own. A pane is not pressed; a pane loading carries aria-busy and holds Skeletons.

Usage

  • Reach for --ruled (or a section heading) first; boxes are for what stands alone.
  • One --double on a view at most; it is the chart's box, not decoration.
  • A page that is read stands on ground, its boxes on card: one paper, so the rule sets the box apart, never a lighter fill.
  • Do not round it, and add no shadow beyond --standing's.

Accessibility

  • A plain div; the heading inside it names it. Use section with a heading when it is a section of the page.
  • The rule is decoration and carries no meaning; a sunken pane's words stay at sem.color.ink-muted or darker (5.4:1 on sunken).
components/pane/component.css
/* Pane — ui/Pane.tsx (paneStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * The box content sits in on a page that is read. Four kinds of box are told
 * apart by their rules, not their fill: the card pane has one ink rule, the
 * sunken pane none (it is the paper's second sheet), and the ruled pane is the
 * broadsheet's section, a heavy rule above and nothing at the sides. Over the
 * map the box is a Surface. */

/* kind="card" (the default): a box ruled in ink, on paper with its grain. */
.wf-pane {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  padding: var(--sem-space-x5);
  border: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-surface);
  background-color: var(--sem-color-card);
  background-image: var(--sem-texture-grain);
  background-repeat: repeat;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}

/* kind="sunken": the paper's second sheet, with no rule: a well, an aside. */
.wf-pane--sunken {
  border: 0;
  background-color: var(--sem-color-sunken);
  background-image: none;
}

/* kind="ruled": a heavy rule above, nothing at the sides, and no inset of its
 * own, so it lines up with the column it is in. Most of a page is this. */
.wf-pane--ruled {
  border: 0;
  border-top: var(--sem-rule-heavy) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  background-color: transparent;
  background-image: none;
  padding: var(--sem-space-x3) 0 0;
}

/* double: a second rule inside the first, the chart's box, for one that
 * matters. */
.wf-pane--double {
  box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-frame);
}

/* standing: a pane on the page on its own rather than in a column of panes.
 * It lifts off the paper a little and takes the wider inset where the width
 * pays for it. */
.wf-pane--standing {
  padding: var(--sem-space-x6);
  box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-surface);
}
.wf-pane--standing.wf-pane--double {
  box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-frame), var(--sem-shadow-surface);
}

/* max-wide: under sem.breakpoint.wide (45rem) the narrow inset comes back. */
@media (max-width: 719.98px) {
  .wf-pane--standing {
    padding: var(--sem-space-x5);
  }
}

PenLoop

PenLoop

Round the best window

Best today 13:00–16:00

Round the hour's reading

1322 WSW · 6 m

The hand · seed 3 (default), 7, 11

13:00 13:00 13:00

PenLoop · night chart (proposed)

Best today 13:00–16:00

The red pen's loop round the one thing on a view that matters (ui/Pen.tsx PenLoop, ui/penPaths.ts loopPath): somebody with the forecast in front of them, circling the hour worth going for.

Anatomy

  • Wrap: .wf-pen-loop — an inline-block round the words, positioned.
  • Mark: .wf-pen-loop__mark — an SVG laid absolutely 12px out across and 8px out down (sem.space.x3, sem.space.x2), its viewBox the words' box plus that pad, so one unit is one pixel; aria-hidden, no pointer events.
  • Stroke: .wf-pen-loop__stroke — loopPath(w / 2, h / 2, box.w / 2 + 7, box.h / 2 + 6, seed): a wobbly ring that runs a little past a full turn and grows as it goes, so its end crosses its start. No fill, sem.color.pen, sem.rule.heavy wide, round caps and joins, at sem.opacity.pen.

Variants

  • Seed: which hand. The same seed draws the same loop every time; 3 is the default.

States

  • Drawing in: the path carries pathLength="1" and stroke-dasharray="1", and sem.animate.ink runs its dash offset from 1 to 0 once.
  • Reduced motion: no animation; the loop is simply there.

Usage

  • One mark on a view, two at most, and on the thing that matters: the best window, the best hour.
  • Never a fill, a control, a status or emphasis.
  • The demo draws the paths statically for its words' measured boxes; the product measures the box and redraws on resize.

Accessibility

  • Decoration over words that already say the same thing: the looped hour is also the best window in the text beside it. The mark is aria-hidden and focusable="false".
  • The pen is a stroke (4.1:1), not words.
components/pen-loop/component.css
/* PenLoop — ui/Pen.tsx (penStyles: wrap, loop, stroke) with ui/penPaths.ts
 * (loopPath), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * The red pen's loop round the one thing on a view that matters: the best
 * hour, the best window. A wobbly ring that overshoots its own start, seeded
 * so the same hand draws the same loop every time, drawn in once as a hand
 * would and simply there for a reader who asks for less motion.
 *
 * The SVG stands clear of the words by 12px across and 8px down
 * (-inset-x-3 -inset-y-2); its viewBox is the box plus that pad, so one user
 * unit is one pixel, and the path is loopPath(w / 2, h / 2, box.w / 2 + 7,
 * box.h / 2 + 6, seed). The path carries pathLength="1" and
 * stroke-dasharray="1", so the ink keyframes draw it whatever its length. */

.wf-pen-loop {
  position: relative;
  display: inline-block;
}

.wf-pen-loop__mark {
  position: absolute;
  top: calc(var(--sem-space-x2) * -1);
  right: calc(var(--sem-space-x3) * -1);
  bottom: calc(var(--sem-space-x2) * -1);
  left: calc(var(--sem-space-x3) * -1);
  overflow: visible;
  pointer-events: none;
}

.wf-pen-loop__stroke {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-pen);
  /* stroke-2: two user units, which are pixels here */
  stroke-width: var(--sem-rule-heavy);
  stroke-linecap: round;
  stroke-linejoin: round;
  opacity: var(--sem-opacity-pen);
  animation: var(--sem-animate-ink);
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .wf-pen-loop__stroke {
    animation: none;
  }
}

@keyframes ink {
  from {
    stroke-dashoffset: 1;
  }
  to {
    stroke-dashoffset: 0;
  }
}

PenNote

PenNote

md · lead (default) · the verdict

Go 13:00–16:00. Four stars on a 6 m.

PenNote · night chart (proposed)

Go 18:00 till dark. Four stars on a 6.5 m.

WSW 14 g22 · cross-shore · HW 13:25

The pen's handwriting in the margin (ui/Pen.tsx PenNote, penNoteStyles): the verdict in a few words, as somebody would write it. "Go 13:00–16:00. Four stars on a 6 m."

Anatomy

  • .wf-pen-note — a paragraph (or a span inside a line), no margin, in sem.font.family.hand (Kalam), sem.font.weight.normal, leading sem.font.line.tight, in sem.color.pen-ink, turned a degree off the level about its top left corner.

Variants

  • --md (the default) — sem.font.size.lead: the verdict.
  • --sm — sem.font.size.prose: the figures in the margin ("WSW 14 g22 · cross-shore · HW 13:25").

States

  • None. A PenUnderline may sit inside it under the word that carries it.

Usage

  • The verdict in a sentence or two, never a paragraph.
  • Kalam is for the pen and nothing else.
  • The Almanac speaks here, plainly, in British and Irish spelling; the Puffin may sign it.

Accessibility

  • Real text, read in order. Pen-ink is 4.9:1 on paper, so it reads as words where the pen's strokes need only be seen.
  • The degree's turn is small enough not to hurt reading; do not turn it more.
components/pen-note/component.css
/* PenNote — ui/Pen.tsx (penNoteStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * The pen's handwriting in the margin: the verdict in a few words, in Kalam,
 * a degree off the level, in the pen's darker ink so it reads as words (4.9:1)
 * where the pen's strokes need only be seen. Never a paragraph. */

.wf-pen-note {
  margin: 0;
  transform: rotate(-1deg);
  transform-origin: top left;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-hand);
  /* md (lead) is the default size; the hand keeps its own weight and leading. */
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-lead);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-tight);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-normal);
  color: var(--sem-color-pen-ink);
}

/* ---- sizes ---- */
.wf-pen-note--sm {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-prose);
}
.wf-pen-note--md {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-lead);
}

PenStrike

PenStrike

Offshore · struck and red, never colour alone

Brandon Bay 0★ SW 10 · cross-off

Sold

€450 Sold

PenStrike · night chart (proposed)

Brandon Bay 0★ SW 10 · cross-off

A stroke of the red pen through what is off (ui/Pen.tsx PenStrike, ui/penPaths.ts strikePath): offshore, sold, cancelled.

Anatomy

  • Wrap: .wf-pen-strike — an inline-block round the words, positioned.
  • Mark: .wf-pen-strike__mark — an SVG over the words' own box, viewBox 0 0 w h; aria-hidden, no pointer events.
  • Stroke: .wf-pen-strike__stroke — strikePath(w, h): from 4% in at 72% down, rising to 96% across at 30% down. sem.color.pen, sem.rule.heavy wide, round caps, at sem.opacity.pen.

Variants

  • None. It takes the size of whatever it strikes: a spot's name, a price.

States

  • Drawing in once with sem.animate.ink (pathLength="1", stroke-dasharray="1"); simply there under reduced motion.

Usage

  • Through a spot that is offshore for this rider, a listing that is sold.
  • Never colour alone: the word is struck *and* red, and the words beside it say why ("cross-off", SOLD).
  • Counts as the view's pen mark.

Accessibility

  • The mark is aria-hidden, so the state must be said in words beside it (offshore, sold) or in the element's label.
components/pen-strike/component.css
/* PenStrike — ui/Pen.tsx (penStyles: wrap, strike, stroke) with
 * ui/penPaths.ts (strikePath), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * A stroke through what is off: offshore, sold, cancelled. It lies over the
 * words' own box (inset-0), its viewBox `0 0 w h`, rising left to right from
 * 4% in at 72% down to 96% across at 30% down: strikePath(w, h). Never colour
 * alone: the word is struck *and* red. Drawn in once; simply there for a
 * reader who asks for less motion. */

.wf-pen-strike {
  position: relative;
  display: inline-block;
}

.wf-pen-strike__mark {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  overflow: visible;
  pointer-events: none;
}

.wf-pen-strike__stroke {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-pen);

  animation: var(--sem-animate-ink);

PenUnderline

PenUnderline

Under the word that carries the note

Go 13:00–16:00. Four stars on a 6 m.

Under a name

Rusheen Bay

In the small hand

Worth it at 13:00. Three stars on a 6.5 m.

PenUnderline · night chart (proposed)

Go 13:00–16:00. Four stars on a 6 m.

A quick stroke of the red pen under the word that carries a note (ui/Pen.tsx PenUnderline, ui/penPaths.ts underlinePath), bowed up a little in the middle.

Anatomy

  • Wrap: .wf-pen-underline — an inline-block round the word, positioned.
  • Mark: .wf-pen-underline__mark — an SVG the word's width and sem.space.x2 tall, hung from the foot of the line box and tucked back up sem.space.x1, because a line box hangs below the letters; viewBox 0 0 w 8; aria-hidden, no pointer events.
  • Stroke: .wf-pen-underline__stroke — underlinePath(0, 3, w), in sem.color.pen, sem.rule.heavy wide, round caps, at sem.opacity.pen.

Variants

  • None. It takes the size of whatever it is under: a word in a PenNote, a spot's name.

States

  • Drawing in once with sem.animate.ink (pathLength="1", stroke-dasharray="1"); simply there under reduced motion.

Usage

  • Under the one word in the pen's note that carries it ("Four stars").
  • Counts as the view's pen mark: one, two at most.
  • Never emphasis in running text, never a link's underline.

Accessibility

  • The mark is aria-hidden; the word says the same thing without it.
components/pen-underline/component.css
/* PenUnderline — ui/Pen.tsx (penStyles: wrap, under, stroke) with
 * ui/penPaths.ts (underlinePath), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * A quick stroke under the word in the pen's note that carries it, bowed up a
 * little in the middle. The SVG is the word's width and 8px tall (h-2), hung
 * from the foot of the line box and tucked back up 4px (top-full
 * -translate-y-1), because a line box hangs below the letters. Its viewBox is
 * `0 0 w 8` and the path underlinePath(0, 3, w). Drawn in once; simply there
 * for a reader who asks for less motion. */

.wf-pen-underline {
  position: relative;
  display: inline-block;
}

.wf-pen-underline__mark {
  position: absolute;
  top: 100%;
  right: 0;
  left: 0;
  height: var(--sem-space-x2);
  transform: translateY(calc(var(--sem-space-x1) * -1));
  overflow: visible;
  pointer-events: none;
}

.wf-pen-underline__stroke {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-pen);
  /* stroke-2: two user units, which are pixels here */
  stroke-width: var(--sem-rule-heavy);
  stroke-linecap: round;
  stroke-linejoin: round;
  opacity: var(--sem-opacity-pen);
  animation: var(--sem-animate-ink);
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .wf-pen-underline__stroke {
    animation: none;
  }
}

@keyframes ink {
  from {
    stroke-dashoffset: 1;
  }
  to {
    stroke-dashoffset: 0;
  }
}

Puffin

Puffin

Sizes · 32, 44 (the menu), 57 (default), 96

32
44
57
96

Signing the note · bob, titled "The Almanac"

Go 13:00–16:00. Four stars on a 6 m.

WSW 14 g22 · cross-shore · HW 13:25

Decorative (aria-hidden) · titled (role img)

Puffin · night chart (proposed)

The Almanac's own bird (ui/Puffin.tsx, puffinStyles), standing on his rock at the foot of the pen's note. He signs the house's word; he does not talk.

Anatomy

  • Root: .wf-puffin — an inline SVG, viewBox 0 0 120 130, size px tall and size × 120 / 130 wide, overflow: visible.
  • Rock: .wf-puffin__rock in sem.color.land, ruled in ink, with a few .wf-puffin__ink-line strokes.
  • Figure: .wf-puffin__figure — the bird without his rock, turning about the foot of its own box.
  • Inks: .wf-puffin__ink (sem.color.ink), __ink-line (ink strokes), __paper (sem.color.ground, ruled in ink: the face and breast), __paper-line (paper strokes: the bill's grooves, the hatch's lines), __pen (sem.color.pen: the bill and feet), __buoy (sem.color.buoy: the bill's base).
  • Hatch: the wing is filled by a pattern of paper lines at 38°; the pattern's line takes __paper-line, the wing's own edge __hatched. Each SVG needs a pattern id of its own.

Variants

  • Size: 57 (the default), 44 (the site menu), 32, 96.
  • --bob — he shifts his weight now and then (sem.animate.bob, a 6s cycle).
  • Decorative (the default) or titled.

States

  • Bobbing, or held still for a reader who asks for less motion.

Usage

  • One puffin on a view at most, beside the pen's note or the menu's line in the Almanac's voice. joke.
  • On the proposed night chart his paper and ink trade places with the page's.

Accessibility

  • Decorative: aria-hidden="true", focusable="false".
  • Where he stands for something, role="img" with an aria-label ("The Almanac").
  • The bob stops under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
components/puffin/component.css
/* Puffin — ui/Puffin.tsx (puffinStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * The Almanac's own bird, on his rock at the foot of the pen's note. He signs
 * the house's word; he does not talk, and there is one of him on a view at
 * most. Drawn in the chart's inks: ink, paper, the pen's red, a buoy's yellow
 * for his beak and land buff for the rock. The drawing (viewBox 0 0 120 130,
 * its stroke widths and two faint ink lines) lives in the SVG; every fill and
 * stroke colour lives here. Height is the size; width is size * 120 / 130. */

.wf-puffin {
  display: inline-block;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  overflow: visible;
}

/* The bird, without his rock: an SVG group turns about its own box only when told to. */
.wf-puffin__figure {
  transform-box: fill-box;
  transform-origin: bottom;
}
/* He shifts his weight now and then. Held still for a reader who asks. */
.wf-puffin--bob .wf-puffin__figure {
  animation: var(--sem-animate-bob);
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .wf-puffin--bob .wf-puffin__figure {
    animation: none;
  }
}

/* ---- the inks ---- */
.wf-puffin__ink {
  fill: var(--sem-color-ink);
}
.wf-puffin__ink-line {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
}
.wf-puffin__paper {
  fill: var(--sem-color-ground);
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
}
.wf-puffin__paper-line {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ground);
}
/* The wing's hatching: the pattern is its fill, so this names a stroke only. */
.wf-puffin__hatched {
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ground);
}
.wf-puffin__pen {
  fill: var(--sem-color-pen);
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
}
.wf-puffin__buoy {
  fill: var(--sem-color-buoy);
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
}
.wf-puffin__rock {
  fill: var(--sem-color-land);
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
}

@keyframes bob {
  0%,
  46%,
  54%,
  100% {
    transform: none;
  }
  50% {
    transform: translateY(-3px) rotate(-2deg);
  }
}

Search field · night chart (proposed)

Hover (held)

Focus-within (held) · hero

A rule to write on, as the chart's "Find a spot…" (ui/SearchField.tsx, searchFieldStyles): no box, an ink line under the words, the placeholder in the body face's italic, the magnifier ahead of it.

Anatomy

  • Field: .wf-search-field on the wrapper that carries aria-busy — a flex row, sem.space.x2 between its parts, sem.space.x0-5 either side, no border but a sem.rule.hairline of sem.color.ink underneath, no fill, sem.color.ink-muted (which the magnifier takes).
  • Magnifier: .wf-search-field__icon — lucide Search, 16 (sem.space.x4), stroke 2, currentColor, aria-hidden.
  • Input: .wf-search-field__input on an <input type="search"> — bare, no platform appearance, Newsreader at sem.font.size.prose, normal weight, sem.color.ink; the placeholder italic in sem.color.ink-muted.
  • Optional trailing part: whatever follows the input inside the field, such as a way to clear it (a quiet icon Button).

Variants

  • lg (the default) — sem.size.control.lg (46) tall: the chart's head.
  • md (--md) — sem.size.control.md (40): a search in a bar.
  • hero (--hero) — the search a page is built around: sem.space.step × 13.5 (54) tall, taller than any other control, on a sem.rule.heavy line, sem.space.x3 between its parts, sem.space.x1 clear on the right, a 20 (sem.space.x5) magnifier, and the words at sem.font.size.lead in normal weight on every pointer.

States

  • Hover: the line goes to sem.color.chart-magenta (.is-hover in the demo).
  • Focus: the one ring round the whole field when its input holds the focus (:focus-within, .is-focus in the demo): sem.ring.width of sem.color.focus, sem.ring.offset clear. The input draws none.
  • Busy (aria-busy="true" on the field): results are on their way; the cursor says progress.
  • Coarse pointer: the field is at least sem.size.touch tall, and the words step to sem.font.size.input (16), except hero, which stays at lead.

Usage

  • The chart's head: the menu, the wordmark, then "Find a spot…" on its rule.
  • A placeholder says what is found ("Find a spot…", "Search listings"), with the ellipsis; there is no visible label.
  • One hero on a page, and only on a page built around its search.
  • Not a form field: a field in a form is a Text input in a Field.

Accessibility

  • A search has no visible label, so it must carry an aria-label; the product's types refuse one without it.
  • type="search" gives the platform's search keyboard and its Escape to clear.
  • aria-busy on the field tells assistive technology results are loading.
  • The rule is ink, 14.6:1; the placeholder ink-muted, 5.8:1 on paper.
components/search-field/component.css
/* Search field — ui/SearchField.tsx (searchFieldStyles), rendered in CSS.
 * Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * A rule to write on, as the chart's "Find a spot…": no box, an ink line
 * under the words, the placeholder in the body face's italic, and the
 * magnifier ahead of it in the muted ink. The line goes magenta under the
 * pointer; the focus draws the one ring round the whole field.
 *
 * `.is-hover` and `.is-focus` hold a state still for the catalog; the product
 * reaches the same rules through :hover and :focus-within. */

.wf-search-field {
  display: flex;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  height: var(--sem-size-control-lg);
  min-width: 0;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x2);
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-x0-5);
  border: 0;
  border-bottom: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-body);
  transition-property: color, background-color, border-color, outline-color;
  transition-duration: var(--sem-duration-fast);
}

.wf-search-field:hover,
.wf-search-field.is-hover {
  border-bottom-color: var(--sem-color-chart-magenta);
}

/* Results are on their way. */
.wf-search-field[aria-busy="true"] {
  cursor: progress;
}

/* A tap target is never shorter than touch, whatever size was asked for. */
@media (pointer: coarse) {
  .wf-search-field {
    min-height: var(--sem-size-touch);
  }
}

/* The one ring, round the field whose input holds the focus (RING_WITHIN). */
.wf-search-field:focus-within,
.wf-search-field.is-focus {
  outline: var(--sem-ring-width) solid var(--sem-color-focus);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-ring-offset);
}

/* The magnifier (lucide Search) in currentColor, the field's muted ink. */
.wf-search-field__icon {
  width: var(--sem-space-x4);
  height: var(--sem-space-x4);
  flex-shrink: 0;
}

.wf-search-field__input {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  width: 100%;
  min-width: 0;
  flex: 1 1 0%;
  align-self: stretch;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 0;
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-body);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-prose);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-prose);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-normal);
  appearance: none;
}
.wf-search-field__input::placeholder {
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
  font-style: italic;
  opacity: 1;
}
/* The field draws the ring; the input draws none (NO_RING). */
.wf-search-field__input:focus-visible {
  outline: none;
}
/* A focused field under 16px makes a phone zoom the page. */
@media (pointer: coarse) {
  .wf-search-field__input {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-input);
    line-height: var(--sem-font-line-input);
  }
}

/* ---- sizes: md (40), lg (46, the default), hero ---- */
.wf-search-field--md {
  height: var(--sem-size-control-md);
}

/* The search a page is built around rather than a control in a bar: taller
 * than any other control, on a heavier rule, in the lead size. */
.wf-search-field--hero {
  height: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 13.5);
  gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
  padding-right: var(--sem-space-x1);
  border-bottom-width: var(--sem-rule-heavy);
}
.wf-search-field--hero .wf-search-field__icon {
  width: var(--sem-space-x5);
  height: var(--sem-space-x5);
}
/* Lead on any pointer (pointer-coarse:text-lead): 19 is past the 16 a phone
 * needs, and this rule outranks the coarse one above. */
.wf-search-field--hero .wf-search-field__input {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-lead);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-lead);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-normal);
}

The broadsheet's section head (ui/SectionHeading.tsx, sectionHeadingStyles): the name in the display face, a rule under it, and on the same line, set right, the figures that sum the section up. The rule is what divides the page; the section needs no box.

Anatomy

  • Root: .wf-section-heading — a wrapping flex row, baseline-aligned, the title and the aside pushed apart (sem.space.x3 across, sem.space.x1 down), sem.space.x1 above the rule. Every side is zeroed first; only the foot is ruled, in sem.color.ink.
  • Title: .wf-section-heading__title — an h2 by default (h1–h4), no margin, sem.font.family.display in sem.color.ink.
  • Aside: .wf-section-heading__aside — a flex row sem.space.x2 apart, in sem.font.family.mono at the caption step, tabular, sem.color.ink-muted: a day's stars and best window, a count.

Variants

  • Size: lead (the default; sem.font.size.lead, a day, a section of a page), --title (sem.font.size.title with its weight and tracking, a page's own head where there is no headline), --kicker (the mono label in muted ink, a group in a list or a menu).
  • Rule: --thin (sem.rule.hairline), thick (the default, sem.rule.heavy), --double (sem.rule.double, a page's foot or the head of what follows a masthead).

States

  • None; it is not interactive.

Usage

  • Most of a page is this, not boxes.
  • The aside is figures, not a sentence: ★★★☆ 12–13, 48, Best Mon. StarGlyphs inside it take the aside's muted ink unless given --ink, which is how the chart sets a day's stars.
  • Pair kicker with thin, title with double; lead with thick.

Accessibility

  • Choose the heading level for the page's outline, not for its size.
  • Stars in the aside carry their own role="img" label ("3 of 5 stars, 4 on the wind alone").
components/section-heading/component.css
/* SectionHeading — ui/SectionHeading.tsx (sectionHeadingStyles), rendered in CSS.
 * Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * The broadsheet's section head: the name in the display face, a rule under
 * it, and on the same line, set right, the figures that sum the section up (a
 * day's stars and best window, a count, a price). The rule divides the page;
 * the section needs no box. */

/* The rule is drawn under only: every side is zeroed first, so a double
   style set on all four sides draws one. Thick (heavy) is the default. */
.wf-section-heading {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: baseline;
  justify-content: space-between;
  column-gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
  row-gap: var(--sem-space-x1);
  padding-bottom: var(--sem-space-x1);
  border: 0 solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  border-bottom-width: var(--sem-rule-heavy);
}

/* ---- rules ---- */
.wf-section-heading--thin {
  border-bottom-width: var(--sem-rule-hairline);
}
.wf-section-heading--thick {
  border-bottom-width: var(--sem-rule-heavy);
}
/* The heaviest: a page's foot, or the head of what follows a masthead. */
.wf-section-heading--double {
  border-style: double;
  border-bottom-width: var(--sem-rule-double);
}

/* ---- the title: lead, the default ---- */
.wf-section-heading__title {
  margin: 0;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-display);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-lead);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-lead);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-lead);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}
/* A page's own head, where there is no headline. */
.wf-section-heading--title .wf-section-heading__title {
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-title);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-title);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-title);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-title);
}
/* A group in a list or a menu: the mono label on a thin rule. */
.wf-section-heading--kicker .wf-section-heading__title {
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-eyebrow);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-eyebrow);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-eyebrow);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-eyebrow);
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
}

/* ---- the aside: figures, not a sentence, set right ---- */
.wf-section-heading__aside {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x2);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-caption);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-caption);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
}

Segmented

Segmented

The dock's switch · Table on

Hover (held) · off, then on

Focus-visible (held)

Disabled item

Stack · on, hovered, disabled

Segmented · night chart (proposed)

Stack

One of a few, all in view (ui/Segmented.tsx, segmentedStyles): the chart's switch, as the dock's TABLE | RIBBON. One capsule ruled in ink, the words in mono capitals, the one that is on filled in ink.

Anatomy

  • Group: .wf-segmented on a role="group" with an aria-label — an inline row in a sem.rule.hairline capsule (sem.radius.full) of sem.color.ink, on sem.color.card.
  • Item: .wf-segmented__item, a <button type="button"> with aria-pressed — sem.size.control.sm tall, sem.space.x3 across, sem.space.x1 between an icon and the words, itself a capsule so the filled one sits round inside the rule. IBM Plex Mono at sem.font.size.label, sem.font.weight.label, tracked sem.font.tracking.label, uppercase, sem.color.ink.

Variants

  • Row (the default) — the capsule, as the dock's switch.
  • Stack (.wf-segmented--stack) — a column of choices: the group becomes a square box ruled in ink (sem.radius.surface), its items sem.size.control.md tall rows, sem.space.x4 across, words to the left, divided by sem.rule.hairline in sem.color.line (none under the last). One row filled.

States

  • On (aria-pressed="true"): filled in sem.color.inverse, words in sem.color.ink-inverse and sem.font.weight.semibold — filled and heavier, never colour alone. It stays filled under the pointer.
  • Hover: sem.color.sunken under an item that is off (.is-hover in the demo).
  • Focus: :focus-visible draws the one ring on the item — sem.ring.width of sem.color.focus, sem.ring.offset clear (.is-focus in the demo).
  • Disabled: sem.color.ink-disabled words, default cursor, no fade, no hover.
  • Coarse pointer: an item is never shorter than sem.size.touch.

Usage

  • Two to four short choices, all in view, exactly one on: how to show the hours (TABLE | RIBBON), how to draw the wind.
  • Name each choice in a word; the group's aria-label says what is being chosen ("Show the hours as").
  • Not an action: pressing an item changes the view, never sends anything. The view's one filled action is still the ink pill beside it.
  • Use the stack in a narrow panel, or when the words are longer than a word.

Accessibility

  • A role="group" of real buttons, each exposing aria-pressed; the group's aria-label is required by the product's types.
  • Each item is in the tab order and pressed with Space or Enter.
  • On is said by fill and weight, so it survives greyscale; paper on ink is 14.6:1.
components/segmented/component.css
/* Segmented — ui/Segmented.tsx (segmentedStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes
 * --sem-* only.
 *
 * The chart's switch, as the dock's TABLE | RIBBON: one capsule ruled in ink,
 * the words in mono capitals, and the one that is on filled in ink. Stacked,
 * a ruled column of choices with one row filled.
 *
 * `.is-hover` and `.is-focus` hold a state still for the catalog; the product
 * reaches the same rules through :hover and :focus-visible. */

.wf-segmented {
  display: inline-flex;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  border: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
  background: var(--sem-color-card);
}

.wf-segmented__item {
  display: inline-flex;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-x1);
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-x3);
  border: 0;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-label);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-label);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-label);
  letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-label);
  text-transform: uppercase;
  white-space: nowrap;
  cursor: pointer;
  touch-action: manipulation;
  transition-property: color, background-color, border-color, outline-color;
  transition-duration: var(--sem-duration-fast);
}

/* A tap target is never shorter than touch. */
@media (pointer: coarse) {
  .wf-segmented__item {
    min-height: var(--sem-size-touch);
  }
}

.wf-segmented__item:not(:disabled):hover,
.wf-segmented__item.is-hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-sunken);
}

/* The one ring: 2px of the chart's magenta, 2px clear (RING). */
.wf-segmented__item:not(:disabled):focus-visible,
.wf-segmented__item.is-focus {
  outline: var(--sem-ring-width) solid var(--sem-color-focus);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-ring-offset);
}

/* Disabled is said in ink and cursor, not a fade (DISABLED). */
.wf-segmented__item:disabled {
  cursor: default;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-disabled);
  opacity: 1;
}

/* The chosen one is filled in ink and set heavier: not colour alone. It stays
 * filled under the pointer. */
.wf-segmented__item[aria-pressed="true"],
.wf-segmented__item[aria-pressed="true"]:not(:disabled):hover,
.wf-segmented__item[aria-pressed="true"].is-hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-inverse);
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-inverse);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
}

/* ---- stack: a column of choices, a ruled list with one row filled ---- */
.wf-segmented--stack {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: stretch;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-surface);
}
.wf-segmented--stack .wf-segmented__item {
  height: var(--sem-size-control-md);
  justify-content: flex-start;
  padding: 0 var(--sem-space-x4);
  border-bottom: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-line);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-surface);
}
.wf-segmented--stack .wf-segmented__item:last-child {
  border-bottom-width: 0;
}

Select · night chart (proposed)

At "any"

Active

Focus (held)

Disabled

A native select in the kit's box (ui/Select.tsx, controlStyles({ kind: "select" })): the platform's own picker, the platform's arrow replaced by a chevron inside the same outline.

Anatomy

  • Box: .wf-control.wf-control--select — the shared field box (hairline in sem.color.line-strong, sem.radius.control, sem.color.card, at least sem.size.touch tall), positioned so the chevron can sit over it.
  • Element: .wf-control__input on a <select> — no platform appearance, Newsreader at sem.font.size.prose, sem.space.x6 clear on the right for the chevron, an ellipsis when the choice is long, a pointer cursor.
  • Chevron: .wf-control__adornment on an inline SVG (lucide ChevronDown, 16, stroke 2) in currentColor, which is the adornment's sem.color.ink-muted; laid sem.space.x3 in from the right, the pointer passing through it. aria-hidden.
  • Shared: the box, the element, the adornment and --active are the .wf-control classes owned by components/text-input/component.css (the product's controlStyles in ui/control.ts). This component links that file and adds only .wf-control--select.

Variants

  • At "any" — the default box.
  • Active (.wf-control--active) — a filter narrowing the results: the border in sem.color.accent.primary and a second hairline inside it, a line and not a fill.

States

  • Hover: the border goes to sem.color.ink (.is-hover in the demo); an active box keeps its accent.
  • Focus: the one ring round the box (:focus-within, .is-focus in the demo).
  • Invalid: sem.color.warn border on sem.color.warn-ground, from aria-invalid="true" or a Field carrying data-invalid.
  • Disabled: sem.color.sunken, a sem.color.line border, sem.color.ink-disabled words, default cursor; the chevron stays ink-muted.
  • Coarse pointer: the words step to sem.font.size.input (16).

Usage

  • For one of many (a spot, a size) where a Segmented would not fit. Two to four short choices all in view are a Segmented instead.
  • A filter's first option is "any" ("Any size"); choosing anything else sets --active.
  • Inside a Field, or with an aria-label in a filter bar.

Accessibility

  • A real <select>: the platform's picker, keyboard and screen-reader behaviour are untouched.
  • The chevron is decoration (aria-hidden="true") and passes the pointer through.
  • Active is said by a second line as well as the accent, so it survives greyscale.
components/select/component.css
/* Select — ui/Select.tsx, controlStyles({ kind: "select" }), rendered in CSS.
 * Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * A native <select>: the platform's own picker, in the kit's box. The box,
 * the element and every state (hover, ring, active, invalid, disabled, the
 * coarse pointer's 16) are the shared `.wf-control` classes in
 * ../text-input/component.css, which the page links first. This file adds
 * only what the select kind adds: the platform's arrow taken off, room for
 * the kit's chevron, and the chevron laid over the right of the box. */

.wf-control--select {
  position: relative;
}

.wf-control--select .wf-control__input {
  appearance: none;
  padding-right: var(--sem-space-x6);
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.wf-control--select .wf-control__input:disabled {
  cursor: default;
}

/* The chevron (lucide ChevronDown, 16) in currentColor: the adornment's
 * ink-muted. The pointer passes through it to the select. */
.wf-control--select .wf-control__adornment {
  position: absolute;
  right: var(--sem-space-x3);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-normal);
  pointer-events: none;
}

Shore compass

Shore compass

Which way the beach faces · sm 16, md 18, lg 20

Facing

The wind against a beach facing WSW · five relations

Shore wind · sm 14 (dock), md 16 (popup), lg 18 (spot page)

In place · the popup's head, the spot page's line

Dublin
SE 123°DublinWSW 15 g26cross-offshore

Shore compass · night chart (proposed)

Which way the beach faces, and how the wind meets it. The mockup's compassSVG and shoreSVG (design/chart/1-the-chart.html); no ui/ primitive yet.

Anatomy

  • Compass: .wf-shore-compass, an SVG on viewBox -10 -10 20 20.
  • __disc: r 8.8, sem.color.card ringed in ink at 0.9.
  • __north: a short ink tick at the top (M0 -8.8V-6.4), so the reader knows which way is up.
  • __face: a group turned by rotate(var(--facing)), holding __sea (a wedge in sem.color.depth pointing out to sea) and __beach (a heavy ink line, 1.7, round caps, across the wedge's foot). --facing is set inline: style="--facing: 247deg".
  • Shore wind: .wf-shore-compass--wind, an SVG on viewBox -9 -9 18 18.
  • __land: the beach below, a band in sem.color.land, with __hatch (fine diagonals in sem.color.line-strong) over it and __shore, an ink line along its top.
  • __wind holding __arrow: the downwind arrow a little above the beach, turned by rotate(calc(var(--from) - var(--facing) + 180deg)), so it is drawn as the wind meets this beach, not as north-up. Set both angles inline: style="--facing: 247deg; --from: 22deg".

Variants

  • Compass sizes: --sm 16 (the popup's head), md 18 (default), --lg 20 (the dock's head).
  • Shore-wind sizes: --sm 14 (a dock cell), md 16 (the popup), --lg 18 (the spot page).
  • Shore relation, on the shore-wind glyph: --onshore, --cross-on, --cross, --cross-off, --offshore. The relation is the angle between the wind and the facing: under 30° onshore, under 70° cross-on, under 110° cross, under 150° cross-off, else offshore.
  • --offshore and --cross-off draw the arrow in sem.color.pen: the wind takes you out, not in.

States

  • None. Both are read-only glyphs; they draw what they are given.

Usage

  • The compass sits beside a spot's name or county (the popup's meta line, the dock's head, the spot page's line "SE 123°"). It describes the beach and never changes with the hour.
  • The shore-wind glyph sits beside a wind reading (the dock's FROM row, the popup's wind line, the spot page's SHORE column) and changes with the hour.
  • Write the shore word beside it where there is room ("cross-offshore"); the pen's colour is a mark, not the message.
  • The pen here is the strike's sibling on the map's light: use it for offshore and cross-off only, never to decorate an onshore arrow.

Accessibility

  • Both glyphs carry role="img", an aria-label and a <title> for the pointer: "Beach faces WSW, 247°"; the shore wind's words, "onshore", "cross-onshore", "cross-shore", "cross-offshore", "offshore".
  • Inside a figure that already says the relation in its own label (the popup's wind line), the glyph's label is not read twice: the parent's role="img" makes it presentational.
  • The arrow's red is never the only signal: the relation is in the label and, where the layout allows, in words beside it.
components/shore-compass/component.css
/* Shore compass — the mockup's compassSVG and shoreSVG (design/chart/1-the-chart.html),
 * in CSS. No ui/ primitive yet; drawn as the signed-off mockup draws them.
 * Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * Two glyphs of one idea, which way the beach faces:
 *   .wf-shore-compass        a paper disc ringed in ink, a north tick, and,
 *                            turned by the facing, the sea (a depth wedge)
 *                            and the beach (a heavy ink line). viewBox -10 -10 20 20.
 *   .wf-shore-compass--wind  the wind against that beach: the beach below (a
 *                            land band, hatched, under an ink line) and an
 *                            arrow blowing downwind over it, in the pen when the
 *                            wind is offshore or cross-off. viewBox -9 -9 18 18.
 *
 * The angles are inline custom properties, not colours:
 *   style="--facing: 247deg"                 the way the beach faces
 *   style="--facing: 247deg; --from: 22deg"  and where the wind comes from
 * Stroke widths are the drawing's geometry, in viewBox units. */

.wf-shore-compass {
  display: inline-block;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  width: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 4.5);
  height: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 4.5);
  vertical-align: middle;
}
.wf-shore-compass--sm {
  width: var(--sem-space-x4);
  height: var(--sem-space-x4);
}
.wf-shore-compass--lg {
  width: var(--sem-space-x5);
  height: var(--sem-space-x5);
}

/* ---- the compass: which way the beach faces ---- */
.wf-shore-compass__disc {
  fill: var(--sem-color-card);
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
  stroke-width: 0.9;
}
.wf-shore-compass__north {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
  stroke-width: 1.3;
}
/* The sea and the beach turn together, by the facing. */
.wf-shore-compass__face {
  transform: rotate(var(--facing, 0deg));
}
.wf-shore-compass__sea {
  fill: var(--sem-color-depth);
}
.wf-shore-compass__beach {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
  stroke-width: 1.7;
  stroke-linecap: round;
}

/* ---- the wind against the beach: 16 by default (the popup), 14 in the dock, 18 on the spot page ---- */
.wf-shore-compass--wind {
  width: var(--sem-space-x4);
  height: var(--sem-space-x4);
}
.wf-shore-compass--wind.wf-shore-compass--sm {
  width: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 3.5);
  height: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 3.5);
}
.wf-shore-compass--wind.wf-shore-compass--lg {
  width: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 4.5);
  height: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 4.5);
}
.wf-shore-compass__land {
  fill: var(--sem-color-land);
}
.wf-shore-compass__hatch {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-line-strong);
  stroke-width: 0.6;
}
.wf-shore-compass__shore {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
  stroke-width: 1.1;
}
/* The arrow sits a little above the beach and points downwind, relative to it. */
.wf-shore-compass__wind {
  transform: translate(0, -2.2px) rotate(calc(var(--from, 0deg) - var(--facing, 0deg) + 180deg));
}
.wf-shore-compass__arrow {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
  stroke-width: 1.4;
  stroke-linecap: round;
  stroke-linejoin: round;
}
/* Off the beach is the pen's: it takes you out, not in. The words say it too. */
.wf-shore-compass--offshore .wf-shore-compass__arrow,
.wf-shore-compass--cross-off .wf-shore-compass__arrow {
  stroke: var(--sem-color-pen);
}

Skeleton

Skeleton

shape="line" · square, as a line of type is

shape="block" · a photo, a chart

shape="circle" · an avatar

A row loading · the holder is aria-busy

Skeleton · night chart (proposed)

block

The shape of what is loading, so the page does not jump when it lands (ui/Skeleton.tsx, skeletonStyles). It says nothing itself.

Anatomy

  • Shape: .wf-skeleton — a block-level span filled with sem.color.line (the hairline's ink, which shows on grained paper where the second sheet does not), breathing with sem.animate.pulse. The caller sets its width.

Variants

  • Line (.wf-skeleton, the default) — sem.space.x3 tall, the field's sem.radius.control: square, as a line of type is.
  • Block (--block) — at least 128px (32 steps) tall, square (sem.radius.surface): a photo, a chart, a pane's worth.
  • Circle (--circle) — sem.size.control.md across, a full circle: an avatar, a light.

States

  • Loading: pulses from 0.45 opacity to whole and back, a second each way.
  • Reduced motion: still (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce); the shape alone says something is coming.

Usage

  • Draw the shape of what will land: as many lines as the row has, at roughly their widths, inside the same box.
  • Swap the whole holder at once when the data lands; do not mix skeletons and real rows.
  • Never as decoration, and never coloured: it is the hairline's ink only.

Accessibility

  • Each shape is aria-hidden. The element that holds them carries aria-busy="true" (and a label where it has none), and drops it when the content lands.
  • Motion is held for a reader who asks for less.
components/skeleton/component.css
/* Skeleton — ui/Skeleton.tsx (skeletonStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * The shape of what is loading, so the page does not jump when it lands. Drawn
 * in the hairline's ink, which shows on grained paper where the second sheet
 * does not, breathing gently; still for a reader who asks for less motion. It
 * says nothing itself: whatever holds it carries aria-busy. */

/* shape="line" (the default): square, as a line of type is. */
.wf-skeleton {
  display: block;
  height: var(--sem-space-x3);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  background: var(--sem-color-line);
  animation: var(--sem-animate-pulse);
}

/* shape="block": a photo, a chart, a pane's worth (128px at the least). */
.wf-skeleton--block {
  height: auto;
  min-height: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 32);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-surface);
}

/* shape="circle": an avatar, a light, a control. */
.wf-skeleton--circle {
  width: var(--sem-size-control-md);
  height: var(--sem-size-control-md);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .wf-skeleton {
    animation: none;
  }
}

/* As ui/theme.css draws it: from just under half, back to whole, alternating. */
@keyframes pulse {
  from {
    opacity: 0.45;
  }
}

A spot on the chart, drawn as the chart draws a light: a ring with the hour's stars in it and an arrow blowing downwind, the spot's name beside it. The mockup's .lt (design/chart/1-the-chart.html); no ui/ primitive yet.

Anatomy

  • Target: .wf-spot-light, a <button> 20px round (sem.space.x5), with no fill or border of its own. On a coarse pointer an invisible sem.size.touch disc grows the target; the glyph stays the same size.
  • Glyph: .wf-spot-light__glyph, an SVG drawn at 60px round the target (viewBox -30 -30 60 60), and inside it:
  • __wind holding __arrow: the path M0 -9.6V-20.5M-3.4 -16.6L0 -21L3.4 -16.6, ink at 1.7, turned by rotate(calc(var(--from) + 180deg)) so it points where the wind blows to. --from is set inline (style="--from: 247deg").
  • __ring: r 7.6, paper ringed in ink at 1.1.
  • __n: the hour's star count, mono semibold at the eyebrow step (10px; the mockup's 9.5), tabular.
  • __strike: the pen's line through the ring, shown only when offshore.
  • Label: .wf-spot-light__label, absolutely placed beside the target, on a paper halo (a text-shadow of sem.color.ground). __name is Fraunces italic semibold at the body step (13px; the mockup's 12); __line is the chart's line in mono medium at the caption step (11px; the mockup's 10, but 11 is the floor for anything not in tracked capitals), in sem.color.chart-magenta: "4★ WSW 14".

Variants

  • --s0: a dashed ring in ink-disabled, the figure in ink-muted at medium weight. Nothing to ride.
  • --s1, --s2: the paper ring (the default).
  • --s3, --s4: filled in ink (sem.color.inverse), the figure in paper.
  • --s5: filled in sem.color.chart-magenta: the best, the one place on the chart that colour says it.
  • --dark: not rated. The ring shaded with sem.color.hatch and ringed in ink-disabled, no figure, the arrow faint; the line muted and starless ("WSW 13").
  • --off: offshore. Struck through in sem.color.pen, the ring and arrow in the pen, the figure and the line in sem.color.pen-ink (the pen's words), and the line ends "· offshore". Struck and red and worded: never colour alone. Combine with the star class (--s2 --off).
  • --xoff: cross-offshore. The arrow in the pen, the line in ink-muted ending "· cross-off".
  • --named: the label shown (a featured spot, or the chart zoomed in far enough to name every light).

States

  • Selected (--sel, with aria-pressed="true"): the label is shown and the light rises over its neighbours.
  • In focus: a container with .wf-spot-light-field--focus dims every light but the selected one to sem.opacity.dot and hides their labels, so the spot in view stands alone.
  • Hover and focus: the glyph scales 1.18 (sem.duration.fast); held still in the demo with .is-hover / .is-focus. Reduced motion drops the transition.
  • Focus-visible: the one ring, sem.ring.width of sem.color.focus, with sem.space.x1-5 clear (the mockup's 6px), so it rounds the ring rather than the 20px target.

Usage

  • One per spot on the map, positioned by the map at the spot's centre.
  • The ring's fill says the stars and nothing else: shape carries the kind, colour carries the reading. Do not tint a light by wind speed.
  • Magenta only at five stars. Do not use --s5 to mean "selected": the selected light is --sel, which keeps its stars' fill.
  • The line is figures: stars, compass point, knots, and the shore word only when the wind is off the beach.
  • The arrow's angle is the only inline style, and it is not a colour.

Accessibility

  • A real <button type="button">; the glyph and the visual label are aria-hidden, and the button carries the whole reading in its aria-label: "Rusheen Bay: 4 stars, WSW 14 knots" or "Brandon Bay: 2 stars, ENE 12 knots, offshore", "Keel Beach: dark, WSW 13 knots".
  • The selected light exposes aria-pressed="true".
  • Offshore is said three ways: the strike, the pen's colour and the word.
  • Contrast: paper on ink 14.6:1, paper on magenta 5.7:1, pen-ink on paper 4.9:1. The label's halo keeps the words readable over sea and land.
  • Touch: the coarse-pointer target is sem.size.touch across.
components/spot-light/component.css
/* Spot light — the spot's light on the chart: the mockup's `.lt`
 * (design/chart/1-the-chart.html). No ui/ primitive yet; drawn as the
 * signed-off mockup draws it. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * A 20px target, with the glyph drawn at 60px round it (viewBox -30 -30 60 60):
 * a ring with the hour's stars in it, an arrow blowing downwind, and beside it
 * the label (the name, and the chart's line in magenta) on a paper halo.
 * Shape carries the kind; the ring's fill carries the stars, and nothing else.
 *
 * The wind is an inline custom property, not a colour: style="--from: 247deg"
 * (where it blows from); the arrow is turned to point where it blows to.
 * `.is-hover` and `.is-focus` hold a state still for the catalog; the product
 * reaches the same rules through :hover and :focus-visible. */

.wf-spot-light {
  position: relative;
  display: inline-block;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  width: var(--sem-space-x5);
  height: var(--sem-space-x5);
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  font: inherit;
  cursor: pointer;
  touch-action: manipulation;
}

/* A finger gets a touch-sized target; the glyph does not grow. */
@media (pointer: coarse) {
  .wf-spot-light::before {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    top: 50%;
    left: 50%;
    width: var(--sem-size-touch);
    height: var(--sem-size-touch);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-full);
    transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
  }
}

.wf-spot-light:focus-visible,
.wf-spot-light.is-focus {
  outline: var(--sem-ring-width) solid var(--sem-color-focus);
  /* The ring clears the glyph, not the 20px target: the mockup's 6px. */
  outline-offset: var(--sem-space-x1-5);
}

/* ---- the glyph, 60px round the 20px target ---- */
.wf-spot-light__glyph {
  position: absolute;
  top: calc(var(--sem-space-x5) * -1);
  left: calc(var(--sem-space-x5) * -1);
  width: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 15);
  height: calc(var(--sem-space-step) * 15);
  overflow: visible;
  pointer-events: none;
  transition-property: transform, opacity;
  transition-duration: var(--sem-duration-fast), var(--sem-duration-base);
}
.wf-spot-light:hover .wf-spot-light__glyph,
.wf-spot-light:focus-visible .wf-spot-light__glyph,
.wf-spot-light.is-hover .wf-spot-light__glyph,
.wf-spot-light.is-focus .wf-spot-light__glyph {
  transform: scale(1.18);
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .wf-spot-light__glyph {
    transition: none;
  }
}

/* The arrow turns by where the wind blows to: from + 180°. */
.wf-spot-light__wind {
  transform: rotate(calc(var(--from, 0deg) + 180deg));
}
.wf-spot-light__arrow {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
  stroke-width: 1.7;
  stroke-linecap: round;
  stroke-linejoin: round;
}
.wf-spot-light__ring {
  fill: var(--sem-color-card);
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink);
  stroke-width: 1.1;
}
.wf-spot-light__n {
  fill: var(--sem-color-ink);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-eyebrow);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
.wf-spot-light__strike {
  display: none;
  stroke: var(--sem-color-pen);
  stroke-width: 1.6;
  stroke-linecap: round;
}

/* ---- the label: the name, then the chart's line, on a paper halo ---- */
.wf-spot-light__label {
  position: absolute;
  top: calc(var(--sem-space-x1) * -1);
  left: var(--sem-space-x5);
  display: none;
  line-height: 1;
  text-align: left;
  white-space: nowrap;
  pointer-events: none;
  /* The halo: the paper round the letters, as a chart clears its soundings. */
  text-shadow:
    0 0 2px var(--sem-color-ground),
    0 0 3px var(--sem-color-ground),
    0 0 5px var(--sem-color-ground),
    0 0 8px var(--sem-color-ground);
}
.wf-spot-light__name {
  display: block;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-display);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  font-style: italic;
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
}
.wf-spot-light__line {
  display: block;
  margin-top: var(--sem-space-x0-5);
  color: var(--sem-color-chart-magenta);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-caption);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
/* Named: a featured spot, or the chart zoomed in far enough to name them all. */
.wf-spot-light--named .wf-spot-light__label,
.wf-spot-light--sel .wf-spot-light__label {
  display: block;
}

/* ---- the stars: the ring's fill says them ---- */
/* 0: a dashed ring, faint. */
.wf-spot-light--s0 .wf-spot-light__ring {
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink-disabled);
  stroke-dasharray: 2 1.6;
}
.wf-spot-light--s0 .wf-spot-light__n {
  fill: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
}
/* 1 and 2: the paper ring (the default). 3 and 4: filled in ink. */
.wf-spot-light--s3 .wf-spot-light__ring,
.wf-spot-light--s4 .wf-spot-light__ring {
  fill: var(--sem-color-inverse);
}
.wf-spot-light--s3 .wf-spot-light__n,
.wf-spot-light--s4 .wf-spot-light__n {
  fill: var(--sem-color-ink-inverse);
}
/* 5: the best, in the chart's magenta. */
.wf-spot-light--s5 .wf-spot-light__ring {
  fill: var(--sem-color-chart-magenta);
  stroke: var(--sem-color-chart-magenta);
}
.wf-spot-light--s5 .wf-spot-light__n {
  fill: var(--sem-color-ink-inverse);
}

/* Dark: not rated. The ring shaded as the dark hours are, no figure. */
.wf-spot-light--dark .wf-spot-light__ring {
  fill: var(--sem-color-hatch);
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink-disabled);
}
.wf-spot-light--dark .wf-spot-light__arrow {
  stroke: var(--sem-color-ink-disabled);
}
.wf-spot-light--dark .wf-spot-light__n {
  display: none;
}
.wf-spot-light--dark .wf-spot-light__line {
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
}

/* Offshore: struck through in the pen, and said in words on the line. */
.wf-spot-light--off .wf-spot-light__ring {
  fill: var(--sem-color-card);
  stroke: var(--sem-color-pen);
  stroke-dasharray: none;
}
.wf-spot-light--off .wf-spot-light__n {
  fill: var(--sem-color-pen-ink);
}
.wf-spot-light--off .wf-spot-light__strike {
  display: inline;
}
.wf-spot-light--off .wf-spot-light__arrow,
.wf-spot-light--xoff .wf-spot-light__arrow {
  stroke: var(--sem-color-pen);
}
.wf-spot-light--off .wf-spot-light__line {
  color: var(--sem-color-pen-ink);
}
/* Cross-off: the arrow in the pen, the line muted with "· cross-off". */
.wf-spot-light--xoff .wf-spot-light__line {
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-muted);
}

/* ---- selected, and the field round it ---- */
.wf-spot-light--sel {
  z-index: 2;
}
/* A field in focus: the selected light stands, the others dim and lose their names. */
.wf-spot-light-field--focus .wf-spot-light:not(.wf-spot-light--sel) .wf-spot-light__glyph {
  opacity: var(--sem-opacity-dot);
}
.wf-spot-light-field--focus .wf-spot-light:not(.wf-spot-light--sel) .wf-spot-light__label {
  display: none;
}

StarGlyphs

StarGlyphs

Slots · five (default), potential (a narrow cell)

StarGlyphs · night chart (proposed)

An hour's stars as the chart draws them (ui/StarGlyphs.tsx, starGlyphsStyles): solid for what the hour is worth for this rider, an outline for what the wind alone would give, and a dot for each of the five it does not reach. The dark is not rated.

Anatomy

  • Root: .wf-star-glyphs — an inline SVG, overflow: visible, aligned to the middle, size px tall and count × size + (count − 1) × gap wide, where the gap is max(1, floor(size / 6)).
  • Solid: .wf-star-glyphs__solid — the chart's five-point star (radius 5), translated to the slot's centre plus 0.4 down and scaled by size / 10.4, filled currentColor.
  • Faded: .wf-star-glyphs__faded — the same star, outlined in currentColor at 0.95 / scale, at sem.opacity.faded.
  • Dot: .wf-star-glyphs__dot — a circle of size × 0.07 at the slot's centre, filled currentColor at sem.opacity.dot.
  • Geometry lives in the SVG; paint lives in the CSS.

Variants

  • Tone: none (the text's own colour), --ink, --inverse (sem.color.ink-inverse, on an ink fill: a selected column, a light), --magenta (sem.color.chart-magenta, the best of the week, once).
  • Slots: five (the default, the chart's way) or potential (stops at the last outline, for a cell too narrow for five; the dark still takes five).
  • Size: 9.5, 10 (the dock), 12 (the default), 14.

States

  • Stars 0 to 5, with the potential at or above them.
  • The dark (null): an empty SVG of the same width, so a row of hours stays in line; its row is hatched (sem.color.hatch), never rated.

Usage

  • Draw stars with this, never with an icon set's stars.
  • Shape carries the difference between solid and outline; tone only repeats it.
  • Magenta for the one best, once a view.

Accessibility

  • role="img" with a label: "3 of 5 stars, 4 on the wind alone", or "Dark: not rated".
  • The outline at half opacity is a mark beside a solid one, never the only carrier of a figure; the label says it in words.
components/star-glyphs/component.css
/* StarGlyphs — ui/StarGlyphs.tsx (starGlyphsStyles), rendered in CSS.
 * Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * An hour's stars as the chart draws them: solid for what the hour is worth
 * for this rider, an outline for what the wind alone would have given, and a
 * small dot for each of the five it does not reach. Shape carries the
 * difference; the tone only repeats it. The dark is not rated: an empty SVG of
 * the same width, so a row of hours stays in line.
 *
 * The geometry is the component's and lives in the SVG: the star path at
 * radius 5, scaled by size / 10.4 and set 0.4 below centre; a gap of
 * max(1, floor(size / 6)); an outline of 0.95 / scale; a dot of size * 0.07.
 * Only paint lives here, and it is currentColor. */

.wf-star-glyphs {
  display: inline-block;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  overflow: visible;
  vertical-align: middle;
}

/* ---- tones: none, by default, is whatever the text round it is ---- */
.wf-star-glyphs--ink {
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
}
/* On an ink fill: a selected column, a light. */
.wf-star-glyphs--inverse {
  color: var(--sem-color-ink-inverse);
}
/* The best of the week, where magenta marks it. */
.wf-star-glyphs--magenta {
  color: var(--sem-color-chart-magenta);
}

/* ---- the three marks ---- */
.wf-star-glyphs__solid {
  fill: currentColor;
}
/* What the wind alone would give: an outline, faded. */
.wf-star-glyphs__faded {
  fill: none;
  stroke: currentColor;
  opacity: var(--sem-opacity-faded);
}
/* A place the hour does not reach. */
.wf-star-glyphs__dot {
  fill: currentColor;
  opacity: var(--sem-opacity-dot);
}

        justify-items: start;
        gap: var(--sem-space-x1);
      }
      .demo__inverse {
        display: inline-flex;
        padding: var(--sem-space-x1) var(--sem-space-x2);
        background: var(--sem-color-inverse);
      }
      /* A run of hours, as the dock's table draws it: the dark hatched, unrated. */
      .demo__hours {
        display: grid;
        width: 100%;
        max-width: var(--sem-container-dialog);
      }
      .demo__hour {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: var(--sem-space-x3);
        padding: var(--sem-space-x1-5) var(--sem-space-x2);
        border-bottom: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-line);
      }
      .demo__hour--dark {
        background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, var(--sem-color-hatch) 0 1px, transparent 1px 4px);
      }
      .demo__ist {
        font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
        font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
        line-height: var(--sem-font-line-body);
        font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-semibold);
        font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
      }
    </style>
  </head>

The chart's box laid over the moving map (ui/Surface.tsx, surfaceStyles): the search, the layers, the starred spots, a spot's popout. Opaque paper with its grain, ruled in ink. On a page that is read, the box is a Pane.

Anatomy

  • Container: .wf-surface — sem.space.x5 inset on every side, sem.color.card with sem.texture.grain, sem.color.ink words.
  • Rule: a sem.rule.hairline border in sem.color.ink, square (sem.radius.surface).
  • Inner line: sem.shadow.frame (three of paper, then one of ink, inset), which with the border makes the double rule.
  • Lift: sem.shadow.surface, listed after the frame.
  • Content is free: the Surface sets no face or size of its own.

Variants

  • Double (the default, rule="double") — the chart's box: border plus frame plus lift.
  • Single (--single, rule="single") — the border and the lift without the inner line, for a box that sits inside another or is small enough that two lines would be most of it.

States

  • None of its own. It is a box, not a control; what is inside carries focus, hover and disabled.

Usage

  • Over the map only. A page that is read uses Pane.
  • Never translucent, never blurred: over the map, paper is opaque.
  • Keep the double rule for the box that stands alone over the map; reach for --single before nesting one double rule inside another.
  • Everything at one layer casts the same sem.shadow.surface; add no other shadow.
  • Tops out at lead type inside (the spot's name) and figure for figures.

Accessibility

  • A plain div. Give it a landmark or a label where it is a region of its own (role="region" with aria-label, or a nav for the site menu).
  • Ink on paper is 14.6:1; the frame is decoration and carries no meaning.
  • In the night chart (proposed) the frame inverts with the paper through the same tokens.
components/surface/component.css
/* Surface — ui/Surface.tsx (surfaceStyles), rendered in CSS. Consumes --sem-* only.
 *
 * The chart's box laid over the moving map: opaque paper with its grain, a
 * hairline of ink round it and, by default, a second line inside it three of
 * paper in (the double rule). Over the map, paper is opaque: a translucent
 * panel would be a second, blurred map. */

.wf-surface {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  padding: var(--sem-space-x5);
  border: var(--sem-rule-hairline) solid var(--sem-color-ink);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-surface);
  background-color: var(--sem-color-card);
  background-image: var(--sem-texture-grain);
  background-repeat: repeat;
  color: var(--sem-color-ink);
  /* rule="double" (the default): the frame's inner line, then the lift. */
  box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-frame), var(--sem-shadow-surface);
}

/* rule="single": a box inside another, or one small enough that two lines
 * would be most of it. The lift stays; only the inner line goes. */
.wf-surface--single {
  box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-surface);
}
